2:124.ar: ۞وَإِذِ ٱبۡتَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ رَبُّهُۥ بِكَلِمَٰتࣲ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّۖ قَالَ إِنِّي جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامࣰ اۖ قَالَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِيۖ قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهۡدِي ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:124.en: And (remember) when his Lord tried Abraham with (His) commands, and he fulfilled them, He said: Lo! I have appointed thee a leader for mankind. (Abraham) said: And of my offspring (will there be leaders)? He said: My covenant includeth not wrong-doers

79:18.ar: فَقُلۡ هَل لَّكَ إِلَىٰٓ أَن تَزَكَّىٰ
79:18.en: And say (unto him): Hast thou (will) to grow (in grace)

6:9.ar: وَلَوۡ جَعَلۡنَٰهُ مَلَكࣰ ا لَّجَعَلۡنَٰهُ رَجُلࣰ ا وَلَلَبَسۡنَا عَلَيۡهِم مَّا يَلۡبِسُونَ
6:9.en: Had we appointed him (Our messenger) an angel, We assuredly had made him (as) a man (that he might speak to men); and (thus) obscured for them (the truth) they (now) obscure

B218EFMby-M.speaker: adnan
B218EFMby-M.speaker_note: continues his own Yasin series; speaks of founding the Imam Development Academy and his Syrian origin
B218EFMby-M.title: Tafseer of Surat Yasin, Part 2 (13-19)
B218EFMby-M.one_line: Indifference as a choice, then the people of the township: messengers rejected out of ego, suspicion of selfless work, and superstition.
B218EFMby-M.summary: He recaps the opening verses: the opposite of a living heart is indifference, normal in youth but a choice in adulthood. The decree that most will not believe follows their own choices, and he separates forgetting from neglect, which even a court recognizes. He pleads with people not to wait until they lose something to value it, and explains why he named the Imam Development Academy after the Quranic sense of imam as a role model whose legacy is followed. He then gives his historical reading of the story of the township: the Antioch region in the Greek-Iranian period under a king who claimed divine lineage and then vanished from the records, which fits the Quranic pattern of peoples who disappear. Through the verses he explains qaryah as a mixed population, the general word for those sent, and the rare sending of two messengers reinforced by a third. The rejection, you are only humans like us, shows that most great conflicts come down to petty ego, as with Abu Jahl's envy. People cannot believe work with no catch, so Muslims must keep their own service free of hidden strings. Finally he dissects superstition: the township blamed the messengers as bad omens, just as communities today blame jinn and the evil eye to avoid facing mental illness and their own failures.

outline.heading: The opposite of a living heart is indifference
outline.gist: He recaps that true life is the life of the heart and its opposite is a life of indifference to what you have been given.

outline.heading: Indifference in youth and the turn to adulthood
outline.gist: Children cannot be expected to zoom out; by adulthood people must, and religion makes the meaning clear though anyone can find it.

outline.heading: Rituals kept as empty skeletons
outline.gist: Muslims manage to fast and pray while living oblivious lives, keeping the acts without their essence, and they feel the emptiness.

outline.heading: The oath and the mission restated
outline.gist: The Prophet does not speak from himself; he was sent with a message that puts people on a clear, straight path.

outline.heading: The word has come true upon most: decree follows choice
outline.gist: When Allah decrees that someone will not find guidance, it is always based on a choice they made, never arbitrary dislike.

outline.heading: Forgetfulness versus neglect
outline.gist: Forgetting once is human; being reminded again and again and still ignoring it is neglect, and indifference is a choice.

outline.heading: Shackles and those who follow the reminder
outline.gist: He revisits the shackled people who look upward and the receptive person who does not want to live oblivious.

outline.heading: Do not wait until you lose something
outline.gist: People wake up only when they lose someone or something precious; the remorse is painful, so cherish it now.

outline.heading: Good tidings and giving life to the dead
outline.gist: Those with reverence for the unseen receive good news, and Allah records what people did and what followed from it.

outline.heading: Imam as a role model: naming the Imam Development Academy
outline.gist: He chose the name despite pushback because imam in the Quran means an exemplar like Ibrahim whose legacy others follow.

outline.heading: The township story: dating it and the apostles view
outline.gist: He dates it about a century before Isa and rejects the view that the messengers were the apostles of Isa.

outline.heading: Antioch, the Greek-Iranian period and Mount Nemrut
outline.gist: He places the story in the Antioch region under a king who claimed divine lineage and built a great temple on Mount Nemrut.

outline.heading: A king who vanishes from the historical record
outline.gist: Historians cannot say what happened to the king; he reads the sudden end as fitting the Quranic account of punished peoples.

outline.heading: Rock-carved cities with no records
outline.gist: The ruins in Arabia of people who carved castles into rock and then left no trace tell the same story the Quran tells.

outline.heading: Strike for them an example
outline.gist: The verse opens the story as an example to be set before the people.

outline.heading: Qaryah: a town of mixed peoples
outline.gist: Citing a Quranic geographical atlas, he says qaryah denotes a population of different backgrounds, fitting the Greek-Iranian setting.

outline.heading: Rasul, nabi and the general word for those sent
outline.gist: Messengers bring new law and prophets do not; the word used here only says they were sent, without specifying which.

outline.heading: Two messengers sent at once
outline.gist: Two messengers to one people is rare in the Quran, the nearest examples being Yahya with Isa and Musa with Harun.

outline.heading: Reinforced by a third: unity among messengers
outline.gist: The third messenger strengthened the others; each had his own signs yet they agreed with one another.

outline.heading: You are only humans like us
outline.gist: People resent being called by someone like them who was chosen for something they were not.

outline.heading: The world's big problems come down to petty ego
outline.gist: Wars and conflicts trace back to an unchecked disease of the heart, as Pharaoh's saga came from one insecure man's arrogance.

outline.heading: Why messengers are human: the test of the ego
outline.gist: Had angels been sent they would have come as men, because the test is whether you can get over yourself and listen.

outline.heading: Abu Jahl's envy
outline.gist: Abu Jahl privately admitted the Prophet was truthful but would not follow him because his rival clan now had a prophet.

outline.heading: Tazkiyah as getting over the self; the Prophet had no ego
outline.gist: Every conflict comes down to something we are too stubborn to get over; the Prophet would give up his ego whenever it solved a problem.

outline.heading: Our only duty is to convey clearly
outline.gist: The messengers answer that Allah knows they were sent and their only obligation is clear conveyance, not control.

outline.heading: People cannot believe there is no catch
outline.gist: Those ruled by ego assume everyone has a hidden motive; real Islamic work seeks its return only after death.

outline.heading: If there are strings attached, say so upfront
outline.gist: Service with hidden expectations is not for Allah; the Prophet's only condition in the pledge was lifelong commitment to the cause.

outline.heading: You are a bad omen to us: superstition as the go-to discredit
outline.gist: Unable to accuse the messengers of anything, the people blamed them for bad luck.

outline.heading: Superstition rises with ignorance; Islam removed it
outline.gist: Superstition correlates inversely with education; the Prophet removed practices like the divining arrows the Arabs carried.

outline.heading: Blaming the evil eye for everything
outline.gist: In his village every misfortune, from not marrying to cancer after decades of smoking, was blamed on envy and the eye.

outline.heading: Not wanting to rock the boat
outline.gist: The message threatened the king and the status quo, and people avoid controversy even when the whole system is built on lies.

outline.heading: Threats of stoning and your omen is within you
outline.gist: The messengers reply that the omen lies with the people themselves, who go beyond all limits when they dislike a message.

outline.heading: Superstition masks mental illness; why we know about envy
outline.gist: Knowing the evil eye exists is meant to make us humble and careful, not to explain results that have clear causes.

outline.heading: Blaming jinn to avoid facing ourselves
outline.gist: It is easier to blame a jinn than admit a family member's anxiety and depression went unnoticed; superstition is what people reach for when they have no argument.

themes.label: Heedlessness (ghaflah) and inattentiveness
themes.note: Indifference is the opposite of the life of the heart, and in adults it is a choice rather than forgetfulness.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Cherish people and blessings before losing them.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions
themes.note: Imam means an exemplar whose legacy is followed, the reason for the academy's name.

themes.label: Quranic stories and their lessons
themes.note: His historical reading of the people of the township and the Quranic pattern of peoples who disappear.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Rejection of messengers and most human conflicts come from petty ego and envy, as with Pharaoh and Abu Jahl.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Real Islamic work has no catch; if there are strings attached, declare them.

themes.label: Superstition, omens and the evil eye
themes.note: Superstition discredits truth, grows with ignorance, and lets communities avoid facing real causes.

themes.label: Mental health, anxiety and emotional wellbeing
themes.note: Blaming jinn and the eye masks anxiety, depression and family failures.

quran.point: Ibrahim made an imam for people: the sense of exemplar behind the record called imam.
Musa told to invite Pharaoh to purify himself: a simple problem of the heart.
Had Allah sent an angel He would have made him a man: the test is accepting a human messenger.

hadith.gist: The Prophet's pledge of allegiance: the only condition was to persevere in serving Allah's cause for life.

maxims: Indifference is a choice
Don't wait until you lose something
Every conflict comes down to stubborn ego
If there's a catch, it's not Islamic work
When you have no argument, run to superstition

stories.who: The king of the Antioch region who claimed divine lineage
stories.point: A powerful ruler who vanished from the records, matching the Quranic pattern of punished peoples.

stories.who: Pharaoh
stories.point: A whole saga rooted in one insecure man's unchecked arrogance.

stories.who: Abu Jahl confessing the Prophet was truthful
stories.point: Years of opposition came from tribal envy, not doubt about the truth.

stories.who: His village's belief in the evil eye
stories.point: Blaming the unseen hides clear causes like smoking or bad behaviour.

contemporary: Imam Development Academy (IDA)
Mount Nemrut in southeastern Turkey
Middle Eastern conflict, global warming and international wars as products of ego
Superstition and exorcism in Muslim communities masking mental illness
takeaways: Treat repeated neglect of what Allah gave you as a choice and correct it.
Value the people and blessings in front of you before you lose them.
Look for the petty ego beneath your conflicts and get over it.
Serve without hidden expectations, or state your conditions openly.
Do not blame jinn or the evil eye for problems with clear causes, especially mental illness.

5:33.ar: إِنَّمَا جَزَٰٓؤُاْ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحَارِبُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَيَسۡعَوۡنَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَسَادًا أَن يُقَتَّلُوٓاْ أَوۡ يُصَلَّبُوٓاْ أَوۡ تُقَطَّعَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَأَرۡجُلُهُم مِّنۡ خِلَٰفٍ أَوۡ يُنفَوۡاْ مِنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ ذَٰلِكَ لَهُمۡ خِزۡيࣱ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَلَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
5:33.en: The only reward of those who make war upon Allah and His messenger and strive after corruption in the land will be that they will be killed or crucified, or have their hands and feet on alternate sides cut off, or will be expelled out of the land. Such will be their degradation in the world, and in the Hereafter theirs will be an awful doom

5:34.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ تَابُواْ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن تَقۡدِرُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ فَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
5:34.en: Save those who repent before ye overpower them. For know that Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

5:78.ar: لُعِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۢ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ عَلَىٰ لِسَانِ دَاوُۥدَ وَعِيسَى ٱبۡنِ مَرۡيَمَۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَواْ وَّكَانُواْ يَعۡتَدُونَ
5:78.en: Those of the Children of Israel who went astray were cursed by the tongue of David, and of Jesus, son of Mary. That was because they rebelled and used to transgress

5:79.ar: كَانُواْ لَا يَتَنَاهَوۡنَ عَن مُّنكَرࣲ فَعَلُوهُۚ لَبِئۡسَ مَا كَانُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ
5:79.en: They restrained not one another from the wickedness they did. Verily evil was that they used to do

5:106.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ شَهَٰدَةُ بَيۡنِكُمۡ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ حِينَ ٱلۡوَصِيَّةِ ٱثۡنَانِ ذَوَا عَدۡلࣲ مِّنكُمۡ أَوۡ ءَاخَرَانِ مِنۡ غَيۡرِكُمۡ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ ضَرَبۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَأَصَٰبَتۡكُم مُّصِيبَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۚ تَحۡبِسُونَهُمَا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ فَيُقۡسِمَانِ بِٱللَّهِ إِنِ ٱرۡتَبۡتُمۡ لَا نَشۡتَرِي بِهِۦ ثَمَنࣰ ا وَلَوۡ كَانَ ذَا قُرۡبَىٰ وَلَا نَكۡتُمُ شَهَٰدَةَ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّآ إِذࣰ ا لَّمِنَ ٱلۡأٓثِمِينَ
5:106.en: O ye who believe! Let there be witnesses between you when death draweth nigh unto one of you, at the time of bequest - two witnesses, just men from among you, or two others from another tribe, in case ye are campaigning in the land and the calamity of death befall you. Ye shall empanel them both after the prayer, and, if ye doubt, they shall be made to swear by Allah (saying): We will not take a bribe, even though it were (on behalf of) a near kinsman nor will we hide the testimony of Allah, for then indeed we should be of the sinful

5:107.ar: فَإِنۡ عُثِرَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنَّهُمَا ٱسۡتَحَقَّآ إِثۡمࣰ ا فَـَٔاخَرَانِ يَقُومَانِ مَقَامَهُمَا مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَحَقَّ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡأَوۡلَيَٰنِ فَيُقۡسِمَانِ بِٱللَّهِ لَشَهَٰدَتُنَآ أَحَقُّ مِن شَهَٰدَتِهِمَا وَمَا ٱعۡتَدَيۡنَآ إِنَّآ إِذࣰ ا لَّمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
5:107.en: But then, if it is afterwards ascertained that both of them merit (the suspicion of) sin, let two others take their place of those nearly concerned, and let them swear by Allah, (saying): Verily our testimony is truer than their testimony and we have not transgressed (the bounds of duty), for them indeed we should be of the evil-doers

5:108.ar: ذَٰلِكَ أَدۡنَىٰٓ أَن يَأۡتُواْ بِٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهَآ أَوۡ يَخَافُوٓاْ أَن تُرَدَّ أَيۡمَٰنُۢ بَعۡدَ أَيۡمَٰنِهِمۡۗ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱسۡمَعُواْۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
5:108.en: Thus it is more likely that they will bear true witness or fear that after their oaths the oaths (of others) will be taken. So be mindful of your duty (to Allah) and hearken. Allah guideth not the froward folk

24:2.ar: ٱلزَّانِيَةُ وَٱلزَّانِي فَٱجۡلِدُواْ كُلَّ وَٰحِدࣲ مِّنۡهُمَا مِاْئَةَ جَلۡدَةࣲۖ وَلَا تَأۡخُذۡكُم بِهِمَا رَأۡفَةࣱ فِي دِينِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ تُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۖ وَلۡيَشۡهَدۡ عَذَابَهُمَا طَآئِفَةࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
24:2.en: The adulterer and the adulteress, scourge ye each one of them (with) a hundred stripes. And let not pity for the twain withhold you from obedience to Allah, if ye believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a party of believers witness their punishment

5:38.ar: وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَٱقۡطَعُوٓاْ أَيۡدِيَهُمَا جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَسَبَا نَكَٰلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
5:38.en: As for the thief, both male and female, cut off their hands. It is the reward of their own deeds, an exemplary punishment from Allah. Allah is Mighty, Wise

24:4.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَرۡمُونَ ٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتِ ثُمَّ لَمۡ يَأۡتُواْ بِأَرۡبَعَةِ شُهَدَآءَ فَٱجۡلِدُوهُمۡ ثَمَٰنِينَ جَلۡدَةࣰ وَلَا تَقۡبَلُواْ لَهُمۡ شَهَٰدَةً أَبَدࣰ اۚ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
24:4.en: And those who accuse honourable women but bring not four witnesses, scourge them (with) eighty stripes and never (afterward) accept their testimony - They indeed are evil-doers

egCfkHpXGo8.speaker: adnan
egCfkHpXGo8.speaker_note: Sheikh Adnan's Ramadan Quranic Themes series; speaks of his emergency medicine training and growing up in Syria
egCfkHpXGo8.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 6: Quranic Themes 2 - Protecting Public Interest
egCfkHpXGo8.one_line: Al-Ma'idah on protecting the collective: the hirabah penalty, the duty to object to wrong, and trustworthy testimony as the basis of hadith.
egCfkHpXGo8.summary: He places Al-Ma'idah in the story of the seven long surahs as the book of covenants, whose commands protect not only the individual's faith, life, wealth, mind and honour but the public as a whole. The West, he argues, has traded public interest for individual freedom, as the pandemic and the endless overdose cycles he saw in emergency medicine show, while good parents restrict children's freedoms out of love. The hirabah verse, the strictest in the Quran, targets those who wage war on society and spread corruption: organized crime, drug networks and rape, which destroy people's safety in their homes, as he saw happen to Syria, and leave neglected youth with no future, a failure he lays partly on the community. The same logic explains why public zina is punished and private sin is left to Allah, and the door of repentance shows the aim is protection, not brutality. The second passage condemns the Children of Israel for staying silent about wrongdoing among them; a community survives only if people gently but firmly object. The last passage sets rules for witnesses to a deathbed bequest, which later became the foundation for judging hadith narrators. He asks people to care about the collective, speak up against wrong and be trustworthy in what they convey.

outline.heading: Public interest as a main purpose of Islam
outline.gist: Protecting the public is one of the central aims of the deen, and Al-Ma'idah has a clear place in the story told by the seven long surahs.

outline.heading: Al-Ma'idah: the covenants and commands
outline.gist: After the job description, its protection and the ethical system, Al-Ma'idah gives the dos and don'ts in roughly fifteen commands addressed to the believers, each followed by commentary.

outline.heading: Protecting the individual
outline.gist: Islam clearly protects each person's freedom of belief, life, wealth, intellect and reputation.

outline.heading: Protecting the collective, and the West's blind spot
outline.gist: Islam also protects the group, while the West has watered this down by putting individual freedom above the public's interest.

outline.heading: The hudud make sense only through public interest
outline.gist: Severe penalties for murder, theft after break-in, public zina and false accusation look like attacks on dignity until you see what they protect.

outline.heading: The pandemic lesson about personal freedom
outline.gist: Until 2019 eating anything was a private freedom, then a single meal made the world sick; some choices threaten everyone and need limits.

outline.heading: Frequent flyers in the emergency department
outline.gist: Patients who overdose every few nights cost the public system, yet suggesting limits on their freedom becomes a political smear.

outline.heading: Restricting freedom as an act of mercy
outline.gist: Loving parents restrict their children's freedom so they can later live well; Allah addresses humanity in a similar way, at a far higher level.

outline.heading: Terror and the value of feeling safe at home
outline.gist: The verse targets those who spread terror; once people stop feeling safe in their homes, a chain of consequences follows.

outline.heading: Open doors in Syria, then lost forever
outline.gist: He grew up sleeping with the doors open and driving to Damascus at night; once that safety was lost, people's ethics and openness changed with it.

outline.heading: Waging war on society: the strictest verse
outline.gist: Those who provoke war and organize ongoing corruption, like racketeering networks of theft, killing and drugs, ruin countries and generations.

outline.heading: No one sits neutral
outline.gist: People begging at traffic lights could have had full lives; everyone contributes either positively or negatively to society.

outline.heading: Neglected youth and our failure
outline.gist: Young people raised amid abuse, addiction and no role models, including Muslim teens already addicted in high school, are failures of the community, not of a 20-year-old.

outline.heading: Corruption weakens the next generation
outline.gist: Bringing war, drugs, prostitution and gambling into a society produces weak families and a weak country that eventually collapses.

outline.heading: The four penalties of hirabah
outline.gist: Execution, crucifixion, amputation of opposite hand and foot, or exile, because the crime threatens public safety and the future of the ummah.

outline.heading: Ask those who have lived through war
outline.gist: Iraqis, Syrians, Yemenis and Palestinians know what war does to families, homes and children's minds.

outline.heading: Fourteen years of war change a people
outline.gist: He avoids returning to Syria to keep his memory of the country before the war; decades of oppression and war have changed its values, and the judge chooses the penalty by the offence.

outline.heading: Rape falls under hirabah
outline.gist: Rape, unlike consensual zina, robs women of safety in public and is treated as terror; the strictness reflects equal care for the public's rights.

outline.heading: Without the collective there is no ummah
outline.gist: Islam rests on the strength of its units, families, communities and countries, and sacrificing them for individual freedom leaves nothing for the future.

outline.heading: The first person to bring drugs to a city
outline.gist: Introducing drugs sends generations in the wrong direction; if that does not feel like a grave crime, we have been numbed.

outline.heading: Private sin versus public sin
outline.gist: Zina is a major sin, but only its public form is punished because it normalizes haram; four witnesses are required and those who spy are themselves punished.

outline.heading: Repentance before capture
outline.gist: Those who reform before they are caught are treated in light of their repentance, because the aim is protecting the community, not brutality.

outline.heading: Cursed by Dawud and Isa for silence
outline.gist: Two prophets of the Children of Israel cursed the disbelievers among them because they did not forbid one another the wrong they committed.

outline.heading: Not wanting to rock the boat
outline.gist: Ignoring an agreed wrong to spare feelings cost them their ethics and their deen, and they continue in loss.

outline.heading: The beer in the masjid
outline.gist: Objecting gently but clearly is how a community protects itself; ignore one man drinking in the masjid and soon the rows will hold cans.

outline.heading: Interlude
Witnesses to a deathbed bequest
outline.gist: Without notaries or records, a dying person's bequest relied on two just witnesses, or two others when travelling.

outline.heading: Held after the prayer to swear
outline.gist: The witnesses must be practising Muslims, kept after salah to swear they will not sell their testimony.

outline.heading: Bribery and replacing sinful witnesses
outline.gist: Large estates invite bribes to change testimony; witnesses later found openly sinful are replaced by others.

outline.heading: Oaths that make witnesses afraid to lie
outline.gist: The replacement witnesses swear their testimony is truer, so that people fear the consequences of a false oath.

outline.heading: Can we trust one another to convey the truth?
outline.gist: From corrupting society to silence about wrong, the third level is the simplest: honest testimony, without which a society has no hope.

outline.heading: The foundation of hadith criticism
outline.gist: This verse became the basis for judging narrators, since the Prophet's life reached us through companions' testimony long before it was widely written down.

outline.heading: The scholar who would not take the hadith
outline.gist: A scholar travelled far to hear a narrator, saw him trick his camel with an empty hand, and left without his hadith; such strictness is why we trust what we narrate.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: The purposes behind Allah's commands (maqasid)
themes.note: Al-Ma'idah's commands protect both the individual and the public, and the public's interest explains the severe penalties.

themes.label: Modernity, secularism, materialism and their effects
themes.note: Western individualism sacrifices public interest to personal freedom, seen in the pandemic and in the overdose cycle.

themes.label: The unlawfulness of harm and protecting others
themes.note: Terror, organized crime, drugs and rape destroy public safety and the next generation, so they are punished most strictly.

themes.label: Youth, their challenges and their role
themes.note: Neglected and abused young people, including Muslim teens addicted in high school, are the community's responsibility.

themes.label: Syria
themes.note: The safety he grew up with and the moral damage of fourteen years of war.

themes.label: Jurisprudence rulings and how to approach fiqh
themes.note: The hirabah penalties, rape, and the difference between public and private zina explained through their purpose.

themes.label: Commanding good and forbidding wrong (amr bil-ma'ruf)
themes.note: Silence about agreed wrongs destroyed the Children of Israel; objecting gently is how a community protects itself.

themes.label: Oaths, promises, trust and loyalty
themes.note: Rules for witnesses and oaths make testimony trustworthy, which a society cannot survive without.

themes.label: Methodology: how to read texts, tafsir method, intellectual approach
themes.note: The testimony verse grounds the science of judging hadith narrators.

quran.point: The penalty of lashing for zina, among the severe penalties he lists
Cutting the hand for theft, among the severe penalties
Four witnesses required and lashing for accusing without them

maxims: No one sits neutral, ever
Either you contribute positively or you contribute negatively
The jama'ah matters too
Once we lost it, we lost it

stories.who: Frequent flyers in the emergency department
stories.point: Unlimited individual freedom can harm both the person and the public.

stories.who: His childhood in Syria
stories.point: Public safety, once lost, changes a people's ethics and relationships for good.

stories.who: The hadith scholar and the narrator who tricked his camel
stories.point: Strict standards of honesty in narrators are why the hadith we have can be trusted.

contemporary: The COVID-19 pandemic as a lesson in the limits of personal freedom
Repeat overdose patients in emergency departments and the cost to the public health system
People begging at traffic lights and addiction downtown
US racketeering laws against organized crime
Wars in Iraq, Syria, Yemen and Palestine
Muslim teenagers addicted to gambling or substances
takeaways: Weigh your freedoms against their effect on the wider public, not only on yourself.
Take responsibility for neglected young people in the community instead of blaming them.
Point out clear wrongs gently but firmly rather than staying silent to avoid discomfort.
Never sell or bend your testimony; be someone whose word can be trusted.
Keep sins private and never normalize haram publicly.

2:284.ar: لِّلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ وَإِن تُبۡدُواْ مَا فِيٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَوۡ تُخۡفُوهُ يُحَاسِبۡكُم بِهِ ٱللَّهُۖ فَيَغۡفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَآءُۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
2:284.en: Unto Allah (belongeth) whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth; and whether ye make known what is in your minds or hide it, Allah will bring you to account for it. He will forgive whom He will and He will punish whom He will. Allah is Able to do all things

3:29.ar: قُلۡ إِن تُخۡفُواْ مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمۡ أَوۡ تُبۡدُوهُ يَعۡلَمۡهُ ٱللَّهُۗ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
3:29.en: Say, (O Muhammad): Whether ye hide that which is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knoweth it. He knoweth that which is in the heavens and that which is in the earth, and Allah is Able to do all things

3:81.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَٰقَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ لَمَآ ءَاتَيۡتُكُم مِّن كِتَٰبࣲ وَحِكۡمَةࣲ ثُمَّ جَآءَكُمۡ رَسُولࣱ مُّصَدِّقࣱ لِّمَا مَعَكُمۡ لَتُؤۡمِنُنَّ بِهِۦ وَلَتَنصُرُنَّهُۥۚ قَالَ ءَأَقۡرَرۡتُمۡ وَأَخَذۡتُمۡ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُمۡ إِصۡرِيۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَقۡرَرۡنَاۚ قَالَ فَٱشۡهَدُواْ وَأَنَا۠ مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
3:81.en: When Allah made (His) covenant with the prophets, (He said): Behold that which I have given you of the Scripture and knowledge. And afterward there will come unto you a messenger, confirming that which ye possess. Ye shall believe in him and ye shall help him. He said: Do ye agree, and will ye take up My burden (which I lay upon you) in this (matter)? They answered: We agree. He said: Then bear ye witness. I will be a witness with you

3:82.ar: فَمَن تَوَلَّىٰ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
3:82.en: Then whosoever after this shall turn away: they will be miscreants

64:16.ar: فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُمۡ وَٱسۡمَعُواْ وَأَطِيعُواْ وَأَنفِقُواْ خَيۡرࣰ ا لِّأَنفُسِكُمۡۗ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
64:16.en: So keep your duty to Allah as best ye can, and listen, and obey, and spend; that is better for your souls. And whoso is saved from his own greed, such are the successful

2:285.ar: ءَامَنَ ٱلرَّسُولُ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡهِ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَۚ كُلٌّ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتِهِۦ وَكُتُبِهِۦ وَرُسُلِهِۦ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيۡنَ أَحَدࣲ مِّن رُّسُلِهِۦۚ وَقَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا وَأَطَعۡنَاۖ غُفۡرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
2:285.en: The messenger believeth in that which hath been revealed unto him from his Lord and (so do) believers. Each one believeth in Allah and His angels and His scriptures and His messengers - We make no distinction between any of His messengers - and they say: We hear, and we obey. (Grant us) Thy forgiveness, our Lord. Unto Thee is the journeying

gjw6rp7sY1U.speaker: adnan
gjw6rp7sY1U.speaker_note: Sheikh Adnan's Ramadan Quranic Themes series; mentions his decades leading taraweeh
gjw6rp7sY1U.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 3: Quranic Themes 2 - The Knowledge of Allah
gjw6rp7sY1U.one_line: Allah's knowledge as lived experience: comfort in His awareness, accountability for nurtured thoughts, and the covenant of the prophets to follow Muhammad.
gjw6rp7sY1U.summary: He approaches Allah's knowledge through how we experience it rather than as a theological puzzle. Knowing that someone is in control is comforting, like a captain on a bumpy flight, and a god with gaps in knowledge would be no god; since Allah created knowledge itself, we accept His foreknowledge alongside our free choice without trying to grasp His essence. The verse at the end of Al-Baqarah teaches that we answer for what settles in the self: a passing thought carries no blame, but one we keep returning to becomes conviction, cools our love for people and shapes behaviour, and groups reinforce mistaken ideas the same way. The Aal-Imran verse about what lies in the chest adds that Allah sees even fleeting thoughts, which should prompt shame, quick repentance and asking where the thought came from. He then presents the covenant Allah took from every prophet to believe in and support Muhammad if he came in their time, explaining how each revelation confirms the last, why the Quran is for every place and era, and why the Prophet's message is humanity's final chance. He closes with the Prophet asking his companions at the Farewell Hajj to testify that he had conveyed the message.

outline.heading: Savouring Ramadan before it passes
outline.gist: Ramadan's closeness to Allah and sense of community pass quickly, so slow down and appreciate them.

outline.heading: The knowledge of Allah as a major theme
outline.gist: Any theme about Allah is major; tonight he looks at verses about how we experience His knowledge rather than its vastness alone.

outline.heading: His knowledge is meant to comfort
outline.gist: Like a captain on a bumpy flight, knowing Allah is aware of all the pain and bloodshed in the world brings comfort rather than controversy.

outline.heading: A god with ignorance would not be God
outline.gist: Allah created knowledge and the faculties by which we learn, so questioning whether He knows the future is really questioning His existence.

outline.heading: Foreknowledge and free choice
outline.gist: We are free and He knows all; we cannot understand His essence, so we cannot understand the essence of His knowledge and accept it as it is.

outline.heading: Interlude
What you reveal or hide in yourselves
outline.gist: The companions were alarmed that they would be held to what is inside them, and the Prophet calmed them without changing the meaning of the verse.

outline.heading: The nafs is where a thought becomes intention
outline.gist: The self is not a space for passing thoughts but where ideas turn into conviction and desire, which later direct behaviour.

outline.heading: A thought allowed to fester: the cooled salam
outline.gist: A stray dislike for a brother is harmless if dismissed, but entertained repeatedly it cools his greetings and stops him forgiving.

outline.heading: Passing thoughts are human; hidden ones are not tax-free
outline.gist: Everyone has stray thoughts, some people far more than others; what is nurtured inside counts whether it is shown or hidden.

outline.heading: How groups reinforce a wrong idea
outline.gist: A person who knows the right path drifts by bouncing his idea off others who agree until it feels right, and the self does the same internally.

outline.heading: Allah sees even fleeting thoughts
outline.gist: What is in the chest is wider and more fluid; we are not accountable for it, but knowing He saw it should bring shame and quick repentance.

outline.heading: Every thought has a root
outline.gist: Ask where a bad thought came from, whether a habitual mistake, a doubt or unhealed pain, and remove the cause instead of ignoring it.

outline.heading: The covenant of the prophets: knowledge of the unseen
outline.gist: Allah tells of a covenant He took from all the prophets, an event we could never know of had He not shared it.

outline.heading: Messenger and prophet: law versus book
outline.gist: A messenger brings his own law; a prophet follows an earlier law, as Dawud's Zabur taught love of Allah and ethics without new law.

outline.heading: Each revelation confirms the one before
outline.gist: Every scripture came confirming its predecessors; where today's Bible agrees with the Quran it is preserved, and where it differs it was changed.

outline.heading: Same theology and ethics, easier rulings
outline.gist: The Quran changed nothing in belief or ethics but brought lighter rulings than earlier communities carried.

outline.heading: Believe in him and support him
outline.gist: Each prophet had to agree to leave what he had and stand with Muhammad if he came in his lifetime, as even Musa would have followed him.

outline.heading: A final message for every place and age
outline.gist: Earlier books addressed particular peoples; the Quran speaks equally to seventh-century Arabia, London, Ontario in 2026 and whoever lives on Mars.

outline.heading: The heavy covenant, witnessed by Allah
outline.gist: Though Allah knew he would not come in their time, the prophets accepted the condition, affirmed the covenant, and Allah witnessed it with them.

outline.heading: Following him inside and out; turning away is defiance
outline.gist: We gather to follow the Prophet in ethics, values and practice, even in appearance; those who turn from this covenant are the defiantly disobedient.

outline.heading: His message was never an afterthought
outline.gist: Allah decreed Muhammad's prophethood from the beginning and made every prophet aware of it.

outline.heading: The prophets in the heavens: has he been sent?
outline.gist: On the night journey the prophets learned the time had come, a sign that the story of humanity is nearing its end.

outline.heading: Humanity's last chance
outline.gist: There will be no more renewals; we must take the Quran as strongly as the Prophet did, live it and carry it to others.

outline.heading: Farewell Hajj: 'O Allah, be my witness'
outline.gist: The Prophet asked what his companions would say when asked about him, and with tears asked Allah to witness that they testified he had conveyed the message.

outline.heading: Outro
Stand with the imam until the end
outline.gist: Taraweeh is about standing and listening; sit or use a chair if needed but stay to the end, and the young especially should seize these years.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Allah's all-encompassing knowledge presented as a source of comfort and of watchfulness over one's own thoughts.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Doubts about foreknowledge and free will are resolved by accepting that Allah's essence and attributes are beyond our grasp.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: We answer for the thoughts we nurture into convictions, not for those that merely pass through.

themes.label: Tazkiyah: purifying and training the self
themes.note: Guarding what the nafs absorbs, refusing to let thoughts fester and tracing them back to their roots.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Ask what mistake, doubt or pain allowed a bad thought in, rather than ignoring it.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: The covenant of all prophets to support Muhammad, the difference between messenger and prophet, and the continuity of revelation.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: The Prophet's finality and his anxiety to have conveyed the message fully, and our duty to follow him inside and out.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: The Quran is the final guidance for every era and must be taken as seriously as the Prophet took it.

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance
themes.note: Taraweeh is about standing with the imam to the end, adapting as needed.

quran.point: Fear Allah as much as you can, listen, obey and spend: the guidance given to the companions alarmed by 2:284
The response 'we hear and we obey' taught to the companions after 2:284

hadith.gist: When the verse about being held to what is in the self was revealed, the companions were alarmed, and the Prophet reassured them and told them to hear and obey.
Had Musa been alive, he would have had no choice but to follow the Prophet.
hadith.source: Bukhari (as he attributes it; the known wording is in Musnad Ahmad)

hadith.gist: On the night journey, at each heaven the prophets learned that Muhammad had been sent.
At the Farewell Hajj the Prophet asked what people would say when asked about him; they said he had conveyed and advised, and he asked Allah to bear witness.
Whoever prays with the imam until he finishes is recorded as having prayed the whole night.

maxims: If I could break him down, he wouldn't be Allah
A floating thought is fine
Just because you hide it doesn't mean it's tax-free
Every thought comes from somewhere
No more corrections, no more renewals, no more iterations

stories.who: A stray dislike for a brother
stories.point: A thought that is entertained repeatedly cools love and blocks forgiveness.

stories.who: The prophets on the night journey
stories.point: Muhammad's sending signalled the final chapter of humanity's story.

stories.who: The Prophet at the Farewell Hajj
stories.point: He carried the burden of being the last messenger and wanted witnesses that he had fulfilled it.

takeaways: Let Allah's knowledge comfort you in hardship instead of turning it into a theological puzzle.
Dismiss stray thoughts quickly and refuse to rehearse resentment until it shapes how you treat people.
When a bad thought appears, repent and ask what weakness, doubt or pain let it in.
Follow the Prophet in values and conduct, not just in appearance, as the final message entrusted to us.
Stand taraweeh with the imam until the end, especially while you are young.

4:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفۡسࣲ وَٰحِدَةࣲ وَخَلَقَ مِنۡهَا زَوۡجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنۡهُمَا رِجَالࣰ ا كَثِيرࣰ ا وَنِسَآءࣰۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِي تَسَآءَلُونَ بِهِۦ وَٱلۡأَرۡحَامَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ رَقِيبࣰ ا
4:1.en: O mankind! Be careful of your duty to your Lord Who created you from a single soul and from it created its mate and from them twain hath spread abroad a multitude of men and women. Be careful of your duty toward Allah in Whom ye claim (your rights) of one another, and toward the wombs (that bare you). Lo! Allah hath been a watcher over you

4:2.ar: وَءَاتُواْ ٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰٓ أَمۡوَٰلَهُمۡۖ وَلَا تَتَبَدَّلُواْ ٱلۡخَبِيثَ بِٱلطَّيِّبِۖ وَلَا تَأۡكُلُوٓاْ أَمۡوَٰلَهُمۡ إِلَىٰٓ أَمۡوَٰلِكُمۡۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حُوبࣰ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
4:2.en: Give unto orphans their wealth. Exchange not the good for the bad (in your management thereof) nor absorb their wealth into your own wealth. Lo! that would be a great sin

4:3.ar: وَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ أَلَّا تُقۡسِطُواْ فِي ٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ فَٱنكِحُواْ مَا طَابَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ مَثۡنَىٰ وَثُلَٰثَ وَرُبَٰعَۖ فَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ أَلَّا تَعۡدِلُواْ فَوَٰحِدَةً أَوۡ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَدۡنَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعُولُواْ
4:3.en: And if ye fear that ye will not deal fairly by the orphans, marry of the women, who seem good to you, two or three or four; and if ye fear that ye cannot do justice (to so many) then one (only) or (the captives) that your right hands possess. Thus it is more likely that ye will not do injustice

4:4.ar: وَءَاتُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ صَدُقَٰتِهِنَّ نِحۡلَةࣰۚ فَإِن طِبۡنَ لَكُمۡ عَن شَيۡءࣲ مِّنۡهُ نَفۡسࣰ ا فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيٓـࣰٔ ا مَّرِيٓـࣰٔ ا
4:4.en: And give unto the women (whom ye marry) free gift of their marriage portions; but if they of their own accord remit unto you a part thereof, then ye are welcome to absorb it (in your wealth)

4:5.ar: وَلَا تُؤۡتُواْ ٱلسُّفَهَآءَ أَمۡوَٰلَكُمُ ٱلَّتِي جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ قِيَٰمࣰ ا وَٱرۡزُقُوهُمۡ فِيهَا وَٱكۡسُوهُمۡ وَقُولُواْ لَهُمۡ قَوۡلࣰ ا مَّعۡرُوفࣰ ا
4:5.en: Give not unto the foolish (what is in) your (keeping of their) wealth, which Allah hath given you to maintain; but feed and clothe them from it, and speak kindly unto them

4:6.ar: وَٱبۡتَلُواْ ٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغُواْ ٱلنِّكَاحَ فَإِنۡ ءَانَسۡتُم مِّنۡهُمۡ رُشۡدࣰ ا فَٱدۡفَعُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِمۡ أَمۡوَٰلَهُمۡۖ وَلَا تَأۡكُلُوهَآ إِسۡرَافࣰ ا وَبِدَارًا أَن يَكۡبَرُواْۚ وَمَن كَانَ غَنِيࣰّ ا فَلۡيَسۡتَعۡفِفۡۖ وَمَن كَانَ فَقِيرࣰ ا فَلۡيَأۡكُلۡ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۚ فَإِذَا دَفَعۡتُمۡ إِلَيۡهِمۡ أَمۡوَٰلَهُمۡ فَأَشۡهِدُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ حَسِيبࣰ ا
4:6.en: Prove orphans till they reach the marriageable age; then, if ye find them of sound judgment, deliver over unto them their fortune; and devour it not by squandering and in haste lest they should grow up Whoso (of the guardians) is rich, let him abstain generously (from taking of the property of orphans); and whoso is poor let him take thereof in reason (for his guardianship). And when ye deliver up their fortune unto orphans, have (the transaction) witnessed in their presence. Allah sufficeth as a Reckoner

4:7.ar: لِّلرِّجَالِ نَصِيبࣱ مِّمَّا تَرَكَ ٱلۡوَٰلِدَانِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبُونَ وَلِلنِّسَآءِ نَصِيبࣱ مِّمَّا تَرَكَ ٱلۡوَٰلِدَانِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبُونَ مِمَّا قَلَّ مِنۡهُ أَوۡ كَثُرَۚ نَصِيبࣰ ا مَّفۡرُوضࣰ ا
4:7.en: Unto the men (of a family) belongeth a share of that which parents and near kindred leave, and unto the women a share of that which parents and near kindred leave, whether it be little or much - a legal share

4:8.ar: وَإِذَا حَضَرَ ٱلۡقِسۡمَةَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينُ فَٱرۡزُقُوهُم مِّنۡهُ وَقُولُواْ لَهُمۡ قَوۡلࣰ ا مَّعۡرُوفࣰ ا
4:8.en: And when kinsfolk and orphans and the needy are present at the division (of the heritage), bestow on them therefrom and speak kindly unto them

4:9.ar: وَلۡيَخۡشَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَوۡ تَرَكُواْ مِنۡ خَلۡفِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّةࣰ ضِعَٰفًا خَافُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ فَلۡيَتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَلۡيَقُولُواْ قَوۡلࣰ ا سَدِيدًا
4:9.en: And let those fear (in their behaviour toward orphans) who if they left behind them weak offspring would be afraid for them. So let them mind their duty to Allah, and speak justly

4:10.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَأۡكُلُونَ أَمۡوَٰلَ ٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ ظُلۡمًا إِنَّمَا يَأۡكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمۡ نَارࣰ اۖ وَسَيَصۡلَوۡنَ سَعِيرࣰ ا
4:10.en: Lo! Those who devour the wealth of orphans wrongfully, they do but swallow fire into their bellies, and they will be exposed to burning flame

4:11.ar: يُوصِيكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِيٓ أَوۡلَٰدِكُمۡۖ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثۡلُ حَظِّ ٱلۡأُنثَيَيۡنِۚ فَإِن كُنَّ نِسَآءࣰ فَوۡقَ ٱثۡنَتَيۡنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثَا مَا تَرَكَۖ وَإِن كَانَتۡ وَٰحِدَةࣰ فَلَهَا ٱلنِّصۡفُۚ وَلِأَبَوَيۡهِ لِكُلِّ وَٰحِدࣲ مِّنۡهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُ مِمَّا تَرَكَ إِن كَانَ لَهُۥ وَلَدࣱۚ فَإِن لَّمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ وَلَدࣱ وَوَرِثَهُۥٓ أَبَوَاهُ فَلِأُمِّهِ ٱلثُّلُثُۚ فَإِن كَانَ لَهُۥٓ إِخۡوَةࣱ فَلِأُمِّهِ ٱلسُّدُسُۚ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ وَصِيَّةࣲ يُوصِي بِهَآ أَوۡ دَيۡنٍۗ ءَابَآؤُكُمۡ وَأَبۡنَآؤُكُمۡ لَا تَدۡرُونَ أَيُّهُمۡ أَقۡرَبُ لَكُمۡ نَفۡعࣰ اۚ فَرِيضَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
4:11.en: Allah chargeth you concerning (the provision for) your children: to the male the equivalent of the portion of two females, and if there be women more than two, then theirs is two-thirds of the inheritance, and if there be one (only) then the half. And to each of his parents a sixth of the inheritance, if he have a son; and if he have no son and his parents are his heirs, then to his mother appertaineth the third; and if he have brethren, then to his mother appertaineth the sixth, after any legacy he may have bequeathed, or debt (hath been paid). Your parents and your children: Ye know not which of them is nearer unto you in usefulness. It is an injunction from Allah. Lo! Allah is Knower, Wise

4:12.ar: ۞وَلَكُمۡ نِصۡفُ مَا تَرَكَ أَزۡوَٰجُكُمۡ إِن لَّمۡ يَكُن لَّهُنَّ وَلَدࣱۚ فَإِن كَانَ لَهُنَّ وَلَدࣱ فَلَكُمُ ٱلرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكۡنَۚ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ وَصِيَّةࣲ يُوصِينَ بِهَآ أَوۡ دَيۡنࣲۚ وَلَهُنَّ ٱلرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكۡتُمۡ إِن لَّمۡ يَكُن لَّكُمۡ وَلَدࣱۚ فَإِن كَانَ لَكُمۡ وَلَدࣱ فَلَهُنَّ ٱلثُّمُنُ مِمَّا تَرَكۡتُمۚ مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ وَصِيَّةࣲ تُوصُونَ بِهَآ أَوۡ دَيۡنࣲۗ وَإِن كَانَ رَجُلࣱ يُورَثُ كَلَٰلَةً أَوِ ٱمۡرَأَةࣱ وَلَهُۥٓ أَخٌ أَوۡ أُخۡتࣱ فَلِكُلِّ وَٰحِدࣲ مِّنۡهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُۚ فَإِن كَانُوٓاْ أَكۡثَرَ مِن ذَٰلِكَ فَهُمۡ شُرَكَآءُ فِي ٱلثُّلُثِۚ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ وَصِيَّةࣲ يُوصَىٰ بِهَآ أَوۡ دَيۡنٍ غَيۡرَ مُضَآرࣲّۚ وَصِيَّةࣰ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَلِيمࣱ‏
4:12.en: And unto you belongeth a half of that which your wives leave, if they have no child; but if they have a child then unto you the fourth of that which they leave, after any legacy they may have bequeathed, or debt (they may have contracted, hath been paid). And unto them belongeth the fourth of that which ye leave if ye have no child, but if ye have a child then the eighth of that which ye leave, after any legacy ye may have bequeathed, or debt (ye may have contracted, hath been paid). And if a man or a woman have a distant heir (having left neither parent nor child), and he (or she) have a brother or a sister (only on the mother's side) then to each of them twain (the brother and the sister) the sixth, and if they be more than two, then they shall be sharers in the third, after any legacy that may have been bequeathed or debt (contracted) not injuring (the heirs by willing away more than a third of the heritage) hath been paid. A commandment from Allah. Allah is Knower, Indulgent

4:13.ar: تِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ يُدۡخِلۡهُ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۚ وَذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
4:13.en: These are the limits (imposed by) Allah. Whoso obeyeth Allah and His messenger, He will make him enter Gardens underneath which rivers flow, where such will dwell for ever. That will be the great success

4:14.ar: وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَيَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَهُۥ يُدۡخِلۡهُ نَارًا خَٰلِدࣰ ا فِيهَا وَلَهُۥ عَذَابࣱ مُّهِينࣱ‏
4:14.en: And whoso disobeyeth Allah and His messenger and transgresseth His limits, He will make him enter Fire, where he will dwell for ever; his will be a shameful doom

4:15.ar: وَٱلَّٰتِي يَأۡتِينَ ٱلۡفَٰحِشَةَ مِن نِّسَآئِكُمۡ فَٱسۡتَشۡهِدُواْ عَلَيۡهِنَّ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنكُمۡۖ فَإِن شَهِدُواْ فَأَمۡسِكُوهُنَّ فِي ٱلۡبُيُوتِ حَتَّىٰ يَتَوَفَّىٰهُنَّ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ أَوۡ يَجۡعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُنَّ سَبِيلࣰ ا
4:15.en: As for those of your women who are guilty of lewdness, call to witness four of you against them. And if they testify (to the truth of the allegation) then confine them to the houses until death take them or (until) Allah appoint for them a way (through new legislation)

4:16.ar: وَٱلَّذَانِ يَأۡتِيَٰنِهَا مِنكُمۡ فَـَٔاذُوهُمَاۖ فَإِن تَابَا وَأَصۡلَحَا فَأَعۡرِضُواْ عَنۡهُمَآۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ تَوَّابࣰ ا رَّحِيمًا
4:16.en: And as for the two of you who are guilty thereof, punish them both. And if they repent and improve, then let them be. Lo! Allah is ever relenting, Merciful

4:17.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلتَّوۡبَةُ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ لِلَّذِينَ يَعۡمَلُونَ ٱلسُّوٓءَ بِجَهَٰلَةࣲ ثُمَّ يَتُوبُونَ مِن قَرِيبࣲ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يَتُوبُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمۡۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
4:17.en: Forgiveness is only incumbent on Allah toward those who do evil in ignorance (and) then turn quickly (in repentance) to Allah. These are they toward whom Allah relenteth. Allah is ever Knower, Wise

4:18.ar: وَلَيۡسَتِ ٱلتَّوۡبَةُ لِلَّذِينَ يَعۡمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَهُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ قَالَ إِنِّي تُبۡتُ ٱلۡـَٰٔنَ وَلَا ٱلَّذِينَ يَمُوتُونَ وَهُمۡ كُفَّارٌۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَعۡتَدۡنَا لَهُمۡ عَذَابًا أَلِيمࣰ ا
4:18.en: The forgiveness is not for those who do ill-deeds until, when death attendeth upon one of them, he saith: Lo! I repent now; nor yet for those who die while they are disbelievers. For such We have prepared a painful doom

4:19.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمۡ أَن تَرِثُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ كَرۡهࣰ اۖ وَلَا تَعۡضُلُوهُنَّ لِتَذۡهَبُواْ بِبَعۡضِ مَآ ءَاتَيۡتُمُوهُنَّ إِلَّآ أَن يَأۡتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةࣲ مُّبَيِّنَةࣲۚ وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۚ فَإِن كَرِهۡتُمُوهُنَّ فَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكۡرَهُواْ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَيَجۡعَلَ ٱللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيۡرࣰ ا كَثِيرࣰ ا
4:19.en: O ye who believe! It is not lawful for you forcibly to inherit the women (of your deceased kinsmen), nor (that) ye should put constraint upon them that ye may take away a part of that which ye have given them, unless they be guilty of flagrant lewdness. But consort with them in kindness, for if ye hate them it may happen that ye hate a thing wherein Allah hath placed much good

4:20.ar: وَإِنۡ أَرَدتُّمُ ٱسۡتِبۡدَالَ زَوۡجࣲ مَّكَانَ زَوۡجࣲ وَءَاتَيۡتُمۡ إِحۡدَىٰهُنَّ قِنطَارࣰ ا فَلَا تَأۡخُذُواْ مِنۡهُ شَيۡـًٔاۚ أَتَأۡخُذُونَهُۥ بُهۡتَٰنࣰ ا وَإِثۡمࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
4:20.en: And if ye wish to exchange one wife for another and ye have given unto one of them a sum of money (however great), take nothing from it. Would ye take it by the way of calumny and open wrong

4:21.ar: وَكَيۡفَ تَأۡخُذُونَهُۥ وَقَدۡ أَفۡضَىٰ بَعۡضُكُمۡ إِلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ وَأَخَذۡنَ مِنكُم مِّيثَٰقًا غَلِيظࣰ ا
4:21.en: How can ye take it (back) after one of you hath gone in unto the other, and they have taken a strong pledge from you

4:22.ar: وَلَا تَنكِحُواْ مَا نَكَحَ ءَابَآؤُكُم مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِلَّا مَا قَدۡ سَلَفَۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ فَٰحِشَةࣰ وَمَقۡتࣰ ا وَسَآءَ سَبِيلًا
4:22.en: And marry not those women whom your fathers married, except what hath already happened (of that nature) in the past. Lo! it was ever lewdness and abomination, and an evil way

4:23.ar: حُرِّمَتۡ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أُمَّهَٰتُكُمۡ وَبَنَاتُكُمۡ وَأَخَوَٰتُكُمۡ وَعَمَّٰتُكُمۡ وَخَٰلَٰتُكُمۡ وَبَنَاتُ ٱلۡأَخِ وَبَنَاتُ ٱلۡأُخۡتِ وَأُمَّهَٰتُكُمُ ٱلَّٰتِيٓ أَرۡضَعۡنَكُمۡ وَأَخَوَٰتُكُم مِّنَ ٱلرَّضَٰعَةِ وَأُمَّهَٰتُ نِسَآئِكُمۡ وَرَبَٰٓئِبُكُمُ ٱلَّٰتِي فِي حُجُورِكُم مِّن نِّسَآئِكُمُ ٱلَّٰتِي دَخَلۡتُم بِهِنَّ فَإِن لَّمۡ تَكُونُواْ دَخَلۡتُم بِهِنَّ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَحَلَٰٓئِلُ أَبۡنَآئِكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِنۡ أَصۡلَٰبِكُمۡ وَأَن تَجۡمَعُواْ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡأُخۡتَيۡنِ إِلَّا مَا قَدۡ سَلَفَۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
4:23.en: Forbidden unto you are your mothers, and your daughters, and your sisters, and your father's sisters, and your mother's sisters, and your brother's daughters and your sister's daughters, and your foster-mothers, and your foster-sisters, and your mothers-in-law, and your step-daughters who are under your protection (born) of your women unto whom ye have gone in - but if ye have not gone in unto them, then it is no sin for you (to marry their daughters) - and the wives of your sons who (spring) from your own loins. And (it is forbidden unto you) that ye should have two sisters together, except what hath already happened (of that nature) in the past. Lo! Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

4:24.ar: ۞وَٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتُ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡۖ كِتَٰبَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ وَأُحِلَّ لَكُم مَّا وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكُمۡ أَن تَبۡتَغُواْ بِأَمۡوَٰلِكُم مُّحۡصِنِينَ غَيۡرَ مُسَٰفِحِينَۚ فَمَا ٱسۡتَمۡتَعۡتُم بِهِۦ مِنۡهُنَّ فَـَٔاتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةࣰۚ وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِيمَا تَرَٰضَيۡتُم بِهِۦ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلۡفَرِيضَةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
4:24.en: And all married women (are forbidden unto you) save those (captives) whom your right hands possess. It is a decree of Allah for you. Lawful unto you are all beyond those mentioned, so that ye seek them with your wealth in honest wedlock, not debauchery. And those of whom ye seek content (by marrying them), give unto them their portions as a duty. And there is no sin for you in what ye do by mutual agreement after the duty (hath been done). Lo! Allah is ever Knower, Wise

4:25.ar: وَمَن لَّمۡ يَسۡتَطِعۡ مِنكُمۡ طَوۡلًا أَن يَنكِحَ ٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ فَمِن مَّا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُم مِّن فَتَيَٰتِكُمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِۚ وَٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِإِيمَٰنِكُمۚ بَعۡضُكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡضࣲۚ فَٱنكِحُوهُنَّ بِإِذۡنِ أَهۡلِهِنَّ وَءَاتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ مُحۡصَنَٰتٍ غَيۡرَ مُسَٰفِحَٰتࣲ وَلَا مُتَّخِذَٰتِ أَخۡدَانࣲۚ فَإِذَآ أُحۡصِنَّ فَإِنۡ أَتَيۡنَ بِفَٰحِشَةࣲ فَعَلَيۡهِنَّ نِصۡفُ مَا عَلَى ٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِۚ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَنۡ خَشِيَ ٱلۡعَنَتَ مِنكُمۡۚ وَأَن تَصۡبِرُواْ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
4:25.en: And whoso is not able to afford to marry free, believing women, let them marry from the believing maids whom your right hands possess. Allah knoweth best (concerning) your faith. Ye (proceed) one from another; so wed them by permission of their folk, and give unto them their portions in kindness, they being honest, not debauched nor of loose conduct. And if when they are honourably married they commit lewdness they shall incur the half of the punishment (prescribed) for free women (in that case). This is for him among you who feareth to commit sin. But to have patience would be better for you. Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

4:26.ar: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمۡ وَيَهۡدِيَكُمۡ سُنَنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ وَيَتُوبَ عَلَيۡكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
4:26.en: Allah would explain to you and guide you by the examples of those who were before you, and would turn to you in mercy. Allah is Knower, Wise

4:27.ar: وَٱللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَن يَتُوبَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَيُرِيدُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلشَّهَوَٰتِ أَن تَمِيلُواْ مَيۡلًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
4:27.en: And Allah would turn to you in mercy; but those who follow vain desires would have you go tremendously astray

4:28.ar: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ أَن يُخَفِّفَ عَنكُمۡۚ وَخُلِقَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ ضَعِيفࣰ ا
4:28.en: Allah would make the burden light for you, for man was created weak

4:29.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَأۡكُلُوٓاْ أَمۡوَٰلَكُم بَيۡنَكُم بِٱلۡبَٰطِلِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَٰرَةً عَن تَرَاضࣲ مِّنكُمۡۚ وَلَا تَقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُمۡ رَحِيمࣰ ا
4:29.en: O ye who believe! Squander not your wealth among yourselves in vanity, except it be a trade by mutual consent, and kill not one another. Lo! Allah is ever Merciful unto you

4:30.ar: وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٰلِكَ عُدۡوَٰنࣰ ا وَظُلۡمࣰ ا فَسَوۡفَ نُصۡلِيهِ نَارࣰ اۚ وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرًا
4:30.en: Whoso doeth that through aggression and injustice, we shall cast him into Fire, and that is ever easy for Allah

4:31.ar: إِن تَجۡتَنِبُواْ كَبَآئِرَ مَا تُنۡهَوۡنَ عَنۡهُ نُكَفِّرۡ عَنكُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمۡ وَنُدۡخِلۡكُم مُّدۡخَلࣰ ا كَرِيمࣰ ا
4:31.en: If ye avoid the great (things) which ye are forbidden, We will remit from you your evil deeds and make you enter at a noble gate

4:32.ar: وَلَا تَتَمَنَّوۡاْ مَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦ بَعۡضَكُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲۚ لِّلرِّجَالِ نَصِيبࣱ مِّمَّا ٱكۡتَسَبُواْۖ وَلِلنِّسَآءِ نَصِيبࣱ مِّمَّا ٱكۡتَسَبۡنَۚ وَسۡـَٔلُواْ ٱللَّهَ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣰ ا
4:32.en: And covet not the thing in which Allah hath made some of you excel others. Unto men a fortune from that which they have earned, and unto women a fortune from that which they have earned. (Envy not one another) but ask Allah of His bounty. Lo! Allah is ever Knower of all things

4:33.ar: وَلِكُلࣲّ جَعَلۡنَا مَوَٰلِيَ مِمَّا تَرَكَ ٱلۡوَٰلِدَانِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبُونَۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ عَقَدَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡ فَـَٔاتُوهُمۡ نَصِيبَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ شَهِيدًا
4:33.en: And unto each We have appointed heirs of that which parents and near kindred leave; and as for those with whom your right hands have made a covenant, give them their due. Lo! Allah is ever Witness over all things

4:34.ar: ٱلرِّجَالُ قَوَّٰمُونَ عَلَى ٱلنِّسَآءِ بِمَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡضَهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ وَبِمَآ أَنفَقُواْ مِنۡ أَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡۚ فَٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ قَٰنِتَٰتٌ حَٰفِظَٰتࣱ لِّلۡغَيۡبِ بِمَا حَفِظَ ٱللَّهُۚ وَٱلَّٰتِي تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ فَعِظُوهُنَّ وَٱهۡجُرُوهُنَّ فِي ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ وَٱضۡرِبُوهُنَّۖ فَإِنۡ أَطَعۡنَكُمۡ فَلَا تَبۡغُواْ عَلَيۡهِنَّ سَبِيلًاۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيࣰّ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
4:34.en: Men are in charge of women, because Allah hath made the one of them to excel the other, and because they spend of their property (for the support of women). So good women are the obedient, guarding in secret that which Allah hath guarded. As for those from whom ye fear rebellion, admonish them and banish them to beds apart, and scourge them. Then if they obey you, seek not a way against them. Lo! Allah is ever High, Exalted, Great

4:35.ar: وَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ شِقَاقَ بَيۡنِهِمَا فَٱبۡعَثُواْ حَكَمࣰ ا مِّنۡ أَهۡلِهِۦ وَحَكَمࣰ ا مِّنۡ أَهۡلِهَآ إِن يُرِيدَآ إِصۡلَٰحࣰ ا يُوَفِّقِ ٱللَّهُ بَيۡنَهُمَآۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا خَبِيرࣰ ا
4:35.en: And if ye fear a breach between them twain (the man and wife), appoint an arbiter from his folk and an arbiter from her folk. If they desire amendment Allah will make them of one mind. Lo! Allah is ever Knower, Aware

4:36.ar: ۞وَٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُشۡرِكُواْ بِهِۦ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۖ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنࣰ ا وَبِذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱلۡجَارِ ذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡجَارِ ٱلۡجُنُبِ وَٱلصَّاحِبِ بِٱلۡجَنۢبِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَمَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَن كَانَ مُخۡتَالࣰ ا فَخُورًا
4:36.en: And serve Allah. Ascribe no thing as partner unto Him. (Show) kindness unto parents, and unto near kindred, and orphans, and the needy, and unto the neighbour who is of kin (unto you) and the neighbour who is not of kin, and the fellow-traveller and the wayfarer and (the slaves) whom your right hands possess. Lo! Allah loveth not such as are proud and boastful

4:37.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَبۡخَلُونَ وَيَأۡمُرُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ بِٱلۡبُخۡلِ وَيَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦۗ وَأَعۡتَدۡنَا لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ عَذَابࣰ ا مُّهِينࣰ ا
4:37.en: Who hoard their wealth and enjoin avarice on others, and hide that which Allah hath bestowed upon them of His bounty. For disbelievers We prepare a shameful doom

4:38.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ أَمۡوَٰلَهُمۡ رِئَآءَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَلَا بِٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۗ وَمَن يَكُنِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ لَهُۥ قَرِينࣰ ا فَسَآءَ قَرِينࣰ ا
4:38.en: And (also) those who spend their wealth in order to be seen of men, and believe not in Allah nor the Last Day. Whoso taketh Satan for a comrade, a bad comrade hath he

4:39.ar: وَمَاذَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ لَوۡ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَأَنفَقُواْ مِمَّا رَزَقَهُمُ ٱللَّهُۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِمۡ عَلِيمًا
4:39.en: What have they (to fear) if they believe in Allah and the Last Day and spend (aright) of that which Allah hath bestowed upon them, when Allah is ever Aware of them (and all they do)

4:40.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَظۡلِمُ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةࣲۖ وَإِن تَكُ حَسَنَةࣰ يُضَٰعِفۡهَا وَيُؤۡتِ مِن لَّدُنۡهُ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
4:40.en: Lo! Allah wrongeth not even of the weight of an ant; and if there is a good deed, He will double it and will give (the doer) from His presence an immense reward

4:41.ar: فَكَيۡفَ إِذَا جِئۡنَا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةِۭ بِشَهِيدࣲ وَجِئۡنَا بِكَ عَلَىٰ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ شَهِيدࣰ ا
4:41.en: But how (will it be with them) when We bring of every people a witness, and We bring thee (O Muhammad) a witness against these

4:42.ar: يَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَوَدُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَعَصَوُاْ ٱلرَّسُولَ لَوۡ تُسَوَّىٰ بِهِمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَلَا يَكۡتُمُونَ ٱللَّهَ حَدِيثࣰ ا
4:42.en: On that day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the messenger will wish that they were level with the ground, and they can hide no fact from Allah

4:43.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَقۡرَبُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأَنتُمۡ سُكَٰرَىٰ حَتَّىٰ تَعۡلَمُواْ مَا تَقُولُونَ وَلَا جُنُبًا إِلَّا عَابِرِي سَبِيلٍ حَتَّىٰ تَغۡتَسِلُواْۚ وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرۡضَىٰٓ أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ أَوۡ جَآءَ أَحَدࣱ مِّنكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡغَآئِطِ أَوۡ لَٰمَسۡتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَلَمۡ تَجِدُواْ مَآءࣰ فَتَيَمَّمُواْ صَعِيدࣰ ا طَيِّبࣰ ا فَٱمۡسَحُواْ بِوُجُوهِكُمۡ وَأَيۡدِيكُمۡۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَفُوًّا غَفُورًا
4:43.en: O ye who believe! Draw not near unto prayer when ye are drunken, till ye know that which ye utter, nor when ye are polluted, save when journeying upon the road, till ye have bathed. And if ye be ill, or on a journey, or one of you cometh from the closet, or ye have touched women, and ye find not water, then go to high clean soil and rub your faces and your hands (therewith). Lo! Allah is Benign, Forgiving

4:44.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ نَصِيبࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ يَشۡتَرُونَ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةَ وَيُرِيدُونَ أَن تَضِلُّواْ ٱلسَّبِيلَ
4:44.en: Seest thou not those unto whom a portion of the Scripture hath been given, how they purchase error, and seek to make you (Muslims) err from the right way

4:45.ar: وَٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِأَعۡدَآئِكُمۡۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَلِيࣰّ ا وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ نَصِيرࣰ ا
4:45.en: Allah knoweth best (who are) your enemies. Allah is sufficient as a Guardian, and Allah is sufficient as a Supporter

4:46.ar: مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلۡكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِۦ وَيَقُولُونَ سَمِعۡنَا وَعَصَيۡنَا وَٱسۡمَعۡ غَيۡرَ مُسۡمَعࣲ وَرَٰعِنَا لَيَّۢا بِأَلۡسِنَتِهِمۡ وَطَعۡنࣰ ا فِي ٱلدِّينِۚ وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ قَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا وَأَطَعۡنَا وَٱسۡمَعۡ وَٱنظُرۡنَا لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ وَأَقۡوَمَ وَلَٰكِن لَّعَنَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُفۡرِهِمۡ فَلَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
4:46.en: Some of those who are Jews change words from their context and say: "We hear and disobey; hear thou as one who heareth not" and "Listen to us!" distorting with their tongues and slandering religion. If they had said: "We hear and we obey: hear thou, and look at us" it had been better for them, and more upright. But Allah hath cursed them for their disbelief, so they believe not, save a few

4:47.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ ءَامِنُواْ بِمَا نَزَّلۡنَا مُصَدِّقࣰ ا لِّمَا مَعَكُم مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن نَّطۡمِسَ وُجُوهࣰ ا فَنَرُدَّهَا عَلَىٰٓ أَدۡبَارِهَآ أَوۡ نَلۡعَنَهُمۡ كَمَا لَعَنَّآ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلسَّبۡتِۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ مَفۡعُولًا
4:47.en: O ye unto whom the Scripture hath been given! Believe in what We have revealed confirming that which ye possess, before We destroy countenances so as to confound them, or curse them as We cursed the Sabbath-breakers (of old time). The commandment of Allah is always executed

4:48.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَغۡفِرُ أَن يُشۡرَكَ بِهِۦ وَيَغۡفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُۚ وَمَن يُشۡرِكۡ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰٓ إِثۡمًا عَظِيمًا
4:48.en: Lo! Allah forgiveth not that a partner should be ascribed unto Him. He forgiveth (all) save that to whom He will. Whoso ascribeth partners to Allah, he hath indeed invented a tremendous sin

4:49.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَهُمۚ بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يُزَكِّي مَن يَشَآءُ وَلَا يُظۡلَمُونَ فَتِيلًا
4:49.en: Hast thou not seen those who praise themselves for purity? Nay, Allah purifieth whom He will, and they will not be wronged even the hair upon a date-stone

4:50.ar: ٱنظُرۡ كَيۡفَ يَفۡتَرُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡكَذِبَۖ وَكَفَىٰ بِهِۦٓ إِثۡمࣰ ا مُّبِينًا
4:50.en: See, how they invent lies about Allah! That of itself is flagrant sin

4:51.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ نَصِيبࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡجِبۡتِ وَٱلطَّٰغُوتِ وَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ أَهۡدَىٰ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ سَبِيلًا
4:51.en: Hast thou not seen those unto whom a portion of the Scripture hath been given, how they believe in idols and false deities, and how they say of those (idolaters) who disbelieve: "These are more rightly guided than those who believe

4:52.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ ٱللَّهُۖ وَمَن يَلۡعَنِ ٱللَّهُ فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُۥ نَصِيرًا
4:52.en: Those are they whom Allah hath cursed, and he whom Allah hath cursed, thou (O Muhammad) wilt find for him no helper

4:53.ar: أَمۡ لَهُمۡ نَصِيبࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡمُلۡكِ فَإِذࣰ ا لَّا يُؤۡتُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ نَقِيرًا
4:53.en: Or have they even a share in the Sovereignty? Then in that case, they would not give mankind even the speck on a date-stone

4:54.ar: أَمۡ يَحۡسُدُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَىٰ مَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦۖ فَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَآ ءَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُم مُّلۡكًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
4:54.en: Or are they jealous of mankind because of that which Allah of His bounty hath bestowed upon them? For We bestowed upon the house of Abraham (of old) the Scripture and wisdom, and We bestowed on them a mighty kingdom

4:55.ar: فَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ ءَامَنَ بِهِۦ وَمِنۡهُم مَّن صَدَّ عَنۡهُۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِجَهَنَّمَ سَعِيرًا
4:55.en: And of them were (some) who believed therein and of them were (some) who turned away from it. Hell is sufficient for (their) burning

4:56.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا سَوۡفَ نُصۡلِيهِمۡ نَارࣰ ا كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتۡ جُلُودُهُم بَدَّلۡنَٰهُمۡ جُلُودًا غَيۡرَهَا لِيَذُوقُواْ ٱلۡعَذَابَۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
4:56.en: Lo! Those who disbelieve Our revelations, We shall expose them to the Fire. As often as their skins are consumed We shall exchange them for fresh skins that they may taste the torment. Lo! Allah is ever Mighty, Wise

4:57.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ سَنُدۡخِلُهُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدࣰ اۖ لَّهُمۡ فِيهَآ أَزۡوَٰجࣱ مُّطَهَّرَةࣱۖ وَنُدۡخِلُهُمۡ ظِلࣰّ ا ظَلِيلًا
4:57.en: And as for those who believe and do good works, We shall make them enter Gardens underneath which rivers flow - to dwell therein for ever; there for them are pure companions - and We shall make them enter plenteous shade

4:58.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡمُرُكُمۡ أَن تُؤَدُّواْ ٱلۡأَمَٰنَٰتِ إِلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهَا وَإِذَا حَكَمۡتُم بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ أَن تَحۡكُمُواْ بِٱلۡعَدۡلِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُم بِهِۦٓۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ سَمِيعَۢا بَصِيرࣰ ا
4:58.en: Lo! Allah commandeth you that ye restore deposits to their owners, and, if ye judge between mankind, that ye judge justly. Lo! comely is this which Allah admonisheth you. Lo! Allah is ever Hearer, Seer

4:59.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱلرَّسُولَ وَأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِ مِنكُمۡۖ فَإِن تَنَٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِي شَيۡءࣲ فَرُدُّوهُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِ إِن كُنتُمۡ تُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۚ ذَٰلِكَ خَيۡرࣱ وَأَحۡسَنُ تَأۡوِيلًا
4:59.en: O ye who believe! Obey Allah, and obey the messenger and those of you who are in authority; and if ye have a dispute concerning any matter, refer it to Allah and the messenger if ye are (in truth) believers in Allah and the Last Day. That is better and more seemly in the end

4:60.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يَزۡعُمُونَ أَنَّهُمۡ ءَامَنُواْ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبۡلِكَ يُرِيدُونَ أَن يَتَحَاكَمُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱلطَّٰغُوتِ وَقَدۡ أُمِرُوٓاْ أَن يَكۡفُرُواْ بِهِۦۖ وَيُرِيدُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ أَن يُضِلَّهُمۡ ضَلَٰلَۢا بَعِيدࣰ ا
4:60.en: Hast thou not seen those who pretend that they believe in that which is revealed unto thee and that which was revealed before thee, how they would go for judgment (in their disputes) to false deities when they have been ordered to abjure them? Satan would mislead them far astray

4:61.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ وَإِلَى ٱلرَّسُولِ رَأَيۡتَ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَنكَ صُدُودࣰ ا
4:61.en: And when it is said unto them: Come unto that which Allah hath revealed and unto the messenger, thou seest the hypocrites turn from thee with aversion

4:135.ar: ۞يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ شُهَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَوِ ٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبِينَۚ إِن يَكُنۡ غَنِيًّا أَوۡ فَقِيرࣰ ا فَٱللَّهُ أَوۡلَىٰ بِهِمَاۖ فَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ ٱلۡهَوَىٰٓ أَن تَعۡدِلُواْۚ وَإِن تَلۡوُۥٓاْ أَوۡ تُعۡرِضُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣰ ا
4:135.en: O ye who believe! Be ye staunch in justice, witnesses for Allah, even though it be against yourselves or (your) parents or (your) kindred, whether (the case be of) a rich man or a poor man, for Allah is nearer unto both (them ye are). So follow not passion lest ye lapse (from truth) and if ye lapse or fall away, then lo! Allah is ever Informed of what ye do

4:62.ar: فَكَيۡفَ إِذَآ أَصَٰبَتۡهُم مُّصِيبَةُۢ بِمَا قَدَّمَتۡ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ ثُمَّ جَآءُوكَ يَحۡلِفُونَ بِٱللَّهِ إِنۡ أَرَدۡنَآ إِلَّآ إِحۡسَٰنࣰ ا وَتَوۡفِيقًا
4:62.en: How would it be if a misfortune smote them because of that which their own hands have sent before (them)? Then would they come unto thee, swearing by Allah that they were seeking naught but harmony and kindness

4:63.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعۡلَمُ ٱللَّهُ مَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡ فَأَعۡرِضۡ عَنۡهُمۡ وَعِظۡهُمۡ وَقُل لَّهُمۡ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ قَوۡلَۢا بَلِيغࣰ ا
4:63.en: Those are they, the secrets of whose hearts Allah knoweth. So oppose them and admonish them, and address them in plain terms about their souls

4:64.ar: وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا لِيُطَاعَ بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ إِذ ظَّلَمُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ جَآءُوكَ فَٱسۡتَغۡفَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱسۡتَغۡفَرَ لَهُمُ ٱلرَّسُولُ لَوَجَدُواْ ٱللَّهَ تَوَّابࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
4:64.en: We sent no messenger save that he should be obeyed by Allah's leave. And if, when they had wronged themselves, they had but come unto thee and asked forgiveness of Allah, and asked forgiveness of the messenger, they would have found Allah Forgiving, Merciful

4:65.ar: فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ حَتَّىٰ يُحَكِّمُوكَ فِيمَا شَجَرَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُواْ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ حَرَجࣰ ا مِّمَّا قَضَيۡتَ وَيُسَلِّمُواْ تَسۡلِيمࣰ ا
4:65.en: But nay, by thy Lord, they will not believe (in truth) until they make thee judge of what is in dispute between them and find within themselves no dislike of that which thou decidest, and submit with full submission

4:74.ar: ۞فَلۡيُقَٰتِلۡ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَشۡرُونَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۚ وَمَن يُقَٰتِلۡ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَيُقۡتَلۡ أَوۡ يَغۡلِبۡ فَسَوۡفَ نُؤۡتِيهِ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
4:74.en: Let those fight in the way of Allah who sell the life of this world for the other. Whoso fighteth in the way of Allah, be he slain or be he victorious, on him We shall bestow a vast reward

4:75.ar: وَمَا لَكُمۡ لَا تُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمُسۡتَضۡعَفِينَ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ وَٱلنِّسَآءِ وَٱلۡوِلۡدَٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَخۡرِجۡنَا مِنۡ هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةِ ٱلظَّالِمِ أَهۡلُهَا وَٱجۡعَل لَّنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ وَلِيࣰّ ا وَٱجۡعَل لَّنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ نَصِيرًا
4:75.en: How should ye not fight for the cause of Allah and of the feeble among men and of the women and the children who are crying: Our Lord! Bring us forth from out this town of which the people are oppressors! Oh, give us from thy presence some protecting friend! Oh, give us from Thy presence some defender

4:76.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱلطَّٰغُوتِ فَقَٰتِلُوٓاْ أَوۡلِيَآءَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۖ إِنَّ كَيۡدَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ كَانَ ضَعِيفًا
4:76.en: Those who believe do battle for the cause of Allah; and those who disbelieve do battle for the cause of idols. So fight the minions of the devil. Lo! the devil's strategy is ever weak

4:80.ar: مَّن يُطِعِ ٱلرَّسُولَ فَقَدۡ أَطَاعَ ٱللَّهَۖ وَمَن تَوَلَّىٰ فَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ حَفِيظࣰ ا
4:80.en: Whoso obeyeth the messenger hath obeyed Allah, and whoso turneth away: We have not sent thee as a warder over them

4:82.ar: أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَۚ وَلَوۡ كَانَ مِنۡ عِندِ غَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِ لَوَجَدُواْ فِيهِ ٱخۡتِلَٰفࣰ ا كَثِيرࣰ ا
4:82.en: Will they not then ponder on the Qur'an? If it had been from other than Allah they would have found therein much incongruity

4:95.ar: لَّا يَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡقَٰعِدُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ غَيۡرُ أُوْلِي ٱلضَّرَرِ وَٱلۡمُجَٰهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ بِأَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡ وَأَنفُسِهِمۡۚ فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُجَٰهِدِينَ بِأَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡ وَأَنفُسِهِمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡقَٰعِدِينَ دَرَجَةࣰۚ وَكُلࣰّ ا وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰۚ وَفَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُجَٰهِدِينَ عَلَى ٱلۡقَٰعِدِينَ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
4:95.en: Those of the believers who sit still, other than those who have a (disabling) hurt, are not on an equality with those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and lives. Allah hath conferred on those who strive with their wealth and lives a rank above the sedentary. Unto each Allah hath promised good, but He hath bestowed on those who strive a great reward above the sedentary

4:96.ar: دَرَجَٰتࣲ مِّنۡهُ وَمَغۡفِرَةࣰ وَرَحۡمَةࣰۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمًا
4:96.en: Degrees of rank from Him, and forgiveness and mercy. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

m6Bptt139qg.speaker: adnan
m6Bptt139qg.title: A Juz A Day, Juz 5: Faith, Family and Community
m6Bptt139qg.one_line: Surah An-Nisa read through faith, family and community: justice and mercy for orphans, women and the vulnerable, and the laws that protect them.
m6Bptt139qg.summary: He frames Surah An-Nisa around one idea: faith builds strong families and strong families build strong communities, and the surah corrects the historic mistreatment of those easiest to exploit, especially women and orphans. Starting from the shared origin of all people in one soul, he moves through the guardianship of orphans' wealth, the bridal gift, kind provision for the feeble-minded, and the inheritance shares, stressing that children, parents and spouses always inherit and condemning the cultural habit of cheating daughters and widows. He shows how the law treats men and women equally in punishment, how repentance must be sincere and prompt, and how marriage should be lived with kindness even through dislike. He presents the divine laws as a lightening of burdens for a weak creation, then names barriers to justice: financial corruption, envy, broken households, showing off and hypocrisy. He closes on trusts given to the deserving, obedience to the Prophet's judgment, striving and sacrifice for the oppressed, and the command to uphold justice even against oneself and one's family. He asks listeners to give every heir their due, treat spouses with dignity, keep good deeds private and read the end of the juz in full.

outline.heading: Opening
Surah An-Nisa: faith, family and community
outline.gist: The surah's thread: faith builds families, families build communities, and it brings justice and mercy to the historically oppressed, especially women and orphans.

outline.heading: Created from one soul: a single human family
outline.gist: A shared origin in Adam should bind people together and make oppression among them unthinkable; ties of kinship are sacred.

outline.heading: Guardians must not exploit orphans' property
outline.gist: The orphan has lost the breadwinner but keeps an inheritance, and the guardian is warned severely against taking advantage of it.

outline.heading: The bridal gift belongs to the woman
outline.gist: The mahr is a right exclusive to women that must not be compromised.

outline.heading: The feeble-minded: provide for them and speak kindly
outline.gist: Do not hand wealth to those who will squander it, but feed, clothe and address them with dignity: a middle path.

outline.heading: Men and women both have a share of inheritance
outline.gist: Inheritance flows from family and faith and has historically been a tool for oppressing those without leverage.

outline.heading: Consuming orphans' wealth is swallowing fire
outline.gist: A stark image of burning from inside and out, aimed especially at those trusted with authority who abuse it.

outline.heading: Children, parents and spouse always inherit
outline.gist: The fractions are detailed, but three categories can never be left out, and cultures that short-change daughters, wives and mothers break Allah's command.

outline.heading: All-Knowing and Forbearing: you have not outsmarted Allah
outline.gist: The closing Names warn that He sees every scheme and only delays punishment hoping for repentance.

outline.heading: The bounds of Allah and the threat of eternal fire
outline.gist: One of the rare places believers are threatened with lasting fire, showing how grave breaking the inheritance laws is.

outline.heading: Indecency: both parties disciplined equally
outline.gist: Unlike historic double standards, the man does not get away while the woman is punished; justice applied unequally is injustice.
