outline.heading: Four witnesses as protection from accusation
outline.gist: The very high burden of proof shields people, especially women, from speculative conviction.

outline.heading: Repentance that is sincere and prompt
outline.gist: Tawbah is accepted from those who slip and quickly return, not from those who plan to sin until death and repent at the last moment.

outline.heading: Women cannot be inherited
outline.gist: The pre-Islamic custom of inheriting a dead man's wives is abolished outright.

outline.heading: No harshness to reclaim the mahr; live with kindness
outline.gist: Making a wife's life miserable to get the bridal gift back is forbidden; the husband is responsible for a marriage of dignity and respect.

outline.heading: You may dislike something in which Allah placed much good
outline.gist: Advice for strained marriages: let emotions settle, build on the positive and see the bigger picture before separating.

outline.heading: The women one may never marry
outline.gist: Father's wives, blood relatives, milk relations, in-laws and stepdaughters are listed as mahram, laying the base for later hijab rules.

outline.heading: Married women and slavery in antiquity
outline.gist: Already married women are off limits; slavery was an ancient institution the law worked to wind down, and later kingdoms did not always uphold Islam's intent.

outline.heading: Marriage, not fornication
outline.gist: Lawful relations require marriage and chastity; no affairs or hookups, because communities rest on families.

outline.heading: Allah wants to lighten your burden: man was created weak
outline.gist: The laws are meant to ease our load, not add to it; a small virus showed how fragile we are.

outline.heading: Themes are a lens, not a limit on the Quran
outline.gist: Tracing one theme per juz is a way to move quickly; every tangent in the Quran has its own purpose and beauty.

outline.heading: Financial corruption as a barrier to justice
outline.gist: Bribery and fraud, common in poorer Muslim lands, are explicitly forbidden and threatened with fire.

outline.heading: Avoid the major sins and the minor ones are wiped away
outline.gist: Focus on cutting out the major sins and Allah promises to clean up the rest and admit you honourably.

outline.heading: Do not covet what others were given; ask of His bounty
outline.gist: For anyone who feels short-changed: each earns a portion, and envy is a social corruption; ask Allah instead.

outline.heading: Men as providers and protectors
outline.gist: The natural order of the household gives men two roles, providing and protecting, which sets families up for success.

outline.heading: Arbitration when a marriage is in trouble
outline.gist: An arbiter from each family; if both want reconciliation Allah brings it, and if not, harm should end with separation.

outline.heading: Worship Allah and be good to parents, kin and neighbours
outline.gist: Kindness to everyone around us is an extension of worship, even toward relatives who wronged us, short of self-harm.

outline.heading: Miserliness and showing off good deeds
outline.gist: Hide good deeds so that Allah is the one who rewards them; praise from people is not sought.

outline.heading: Allah wrongs no one by a speck of dust
outline.gist: He multiplies every good and does not commit even the smallest injustice imaginable.

outline.heading: Twisting words to belittle the message
outline.gist: Some in Medina's Jewish community distorted words to mock the religion; had they said we hear and obey, it would have been better.

outline.heading: Shirk, the sin that is not forgiven
outline.gist: Allah forgives anything less than associating partners with Him.

outline.heading: Envy of what Allah gave the Prophet; fire and garden
outline.gist: At the core of rejection is jealousy; renewed skins in the fire contrast with cool shade and pure spouses in paradise.

outline.heading: Return trusts to their owners; judge with justice
outline.gist: Positions go to those with merit and judgments must be just; justice and meritocracy are what a community's trust rests on.

outline.heading: Obey those in authority and refer disputes to Allah and His Messenger
outline.gist: A merit-based order needs respected authority and a final reference point for resolving disputes.

outline.heading: Hypocrites exposed by refusing the Prophet's judgment
outline.gist: True faith means accepting the Prophet's decision with no resistance in the heart; his sunnah is authoritative.

outline.heading: Fighting to rescue the oppressed
outline.gist: Armed struggle, under legitimate authority, exists to rescue those crying out for help, while today we watch helplessly as our brothers and sisters are massacred.

outline.heading: The Prophet is not a policeman over people
outline.gist: Obeying the Messenger is obeying Allah; our job is to remind, and judgment belongs to Allah.

outline.heading: Ponder the Quran: no inconsistency in it
outline.gist: Had it come from other than Allah, people would find many contradictions in it.

outline.heading: Interlude
Those who strive are not equal to those who sit back
outline.gist: Those who give their wealth, time and effort for Allah's cause are raised in rank above those who do nothing.

outline.heading: Uphold justice even against yourself and your family
outline.gist: After all the family rights, the surah makes justice for Allah's sake override self-interest and kinship: the true sign of taqwa and iman.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Family
themes.note: Faith builds families and families build communities; the surah's rulings on orphans, inheritance and marriage protect the household.

themes.label: Justice
themes.note: Inheritance must reach every heir and punishment must apply equally to men and women; unequal justice is injustice.

themes.label: Justice
themes.note: Trusts to the deserving, just judgment, rescuing the oppressed, and justice even against oneself and one's relatives.

themes.label: Marriage
themes.note: Kindness and dignity toward wives, patience through dislike, the mahram list, the man's role and arbitration before divorce.

themes.label: Community
themes.note: Barriers to a healthy community: financial corruption, envy, showing off and distortion of the message.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance
themes.note: Repentance is for sincere, quick returns, not a last-minute game played after a lifetime of sin.

themes.label: Sins
themes.note: Avoiding major sins brings forgiveness of minor ones.

themes.label: Sincerity
themes.note: Good deeds are hidden so the reward is sought from Allah alone.

themes.label: Hypocrisy
themes.note: The hypocrites' claim of faith was exposed when they would not accept the Prophet's judgment.

hadith.gist: Seek help in fulfilling your affairs by keeping them private

maxims: Faith builds families; families build communities
Justice has to be equally applied, otherwise it becomes injustice
The laws are here to lighten our burdens
The Prophet is not a policeman
contemporary: Muslim cultures that short-change daughters, wives and mothers of their inheritance
Bribery and financial corruption in poorer Muslim countries
COVID as a reminder of human weakness
Muslims being massacred today while others watch helplessly
takeaways: Give every heir, especially daughters, wives and mothers, their full inheritance
In a strained marriage, calm down and look for the good before separating
Focus on cutting out major sins and trust Allah with the rest
Keep your good deeds private
Uphold justice even when it costs you or your family

7:27.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ لَا يَفۡتِنَنَّكُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ كَمَآ أَخۡرَجَ أَبَوَيۡكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ يَنزِعُ عَنۡهُمَا لِبَاسَهُمَا لِيُرِيَهُمَا سَوۡءَٰتِهِمَآۚ إِنَّهُۥ يَرَىٰكُمۡ هُوَ وَقَبِيلُهُۥ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ لَا تَرَوۡنَهُمۡۗ إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلشَّيَٰطِينَ أَوۡلِيَآءَ لِلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
7:27.en: O Children of Adam! Let not Satan seduce you as he caused your (first) parents to go forth from the Garden and tore off from them their robe (of innocence) that he might manifest their shame to them. Lo! he seeth you, he and his tribe, from whence ye see him not. Lo! We have made the devils protecting friends for those who believe not

2:268.ar: ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ يَعِدُكُمُ ٱلۡفَقۡرَ وَيَأۡمُرُكُم بِٱلۡفَحۡشَآءِۖ وَٱللَّهُ يَعِدُكُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣰ مِّنۡهُ وَفَضۡلࣰ اۗ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
2:268.en: The devil promiseth you destitution and enjoineth on you lewdness. But Allah promiseth you forgiveness from Himself with bounty. Allah is All-Embracing, All-knowing

3:155.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوۡاْ مِنكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡجَمۡعَانِ إِنَّمَا ٱسۡتَزَلَّهُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ بِبَعۡضِ مَا كَسَبُواْۖ وَلَقَدۡ عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنۡهُمۡۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمࣱ‏
3:155.en: Lo! those of you who turned back on the day when the two hosts met, Satan alone it was who caused them to backslide, because of some of that which they have earned. Now Allah hath forgiven them. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Clement

58:19.ar: ٱسۡتَحۡوَذَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ فَأَنسَىٰهُمۡ ذِكۡرَ ٱللَّهِۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ حِزۡبُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۚ أَلَآ إِنَّ حِزۡبَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرُونَ
58:19.en: The devil hath engrossed them and so hath caused them to forget remembrance of Allah. They are the devil's party. Lo! is it not the devil's party who will be the losers

17:62.ar: قَالَ أَرَءَيۡتَكَ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كَرَّمۡتَ عَلَيَّ لَئِنۡ أَخَّرۡتَنِ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ لَأَحۡتَنِكَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
17:62.en: He said: Seest Thou this (creature) whom Thou hast honoured above me, if Thou give me grace until the Day of Resurrection I verily will seize his seed, save but a few

17:63.ar: قَالَ ٱذۡهَبۡ فَمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنۡهُمۡ فَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ جَزَآؤُكُمۡ جَزَآءࣰ مَّوۡفُورࣰ ا
17:63.en: He said: Go, and whosoever of them followeth thee - lo! hell will be your payment, ample payment

17:64.ar: وَٱسۡتَفۡزِزۡ مَنِ ٱسۡتَطَعۡتَ مِنۡهُم بِصَوۡتِكَ وَأَجۡلِبۡ عَلَيۡهِم بِخَيۡلِكَ وَرَجِلِكَ وَشَارِكۡهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡوَٰلِ وَٱلۡأَوۡلَٰدِ وَعِدۡهُمۡۚ وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ إِلَّا غُرُورًا
17:64.en: And excite any of them whom thou canst with thy voice, and urge thy horse and foot against them, and be a partner in their wealth and children, and promise them. Satan promiseth them only to deceive

17:65.ar: إِنَّ عِبَادِي لَيۡسَ لَكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ سُلۡطَٰنࣱۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِرَبِّكَ وَكِيلࣰ ا
17:65.en: Lo! My (faithful) bondmen - over them thou hast no power, and thy Lord sufficeth as (their) guardian

35:6.ar: إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ لَكُمۡ عَدُوࣱّ فَٱتَّخِذُوهُ عَدُوًّاۚ إِنَّمَا يَدۡعُواْ حِزۡبَهُۥ لِيَكُونُواْ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
35:6.en: Lo! the devil is an enemy for you, so treat him as an enemy. He only summoneth his faction to be owners of the flaming Fire

4:76.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱلطَّٰغُوتِ فَقَٰتِلُوٓاْ أَوۡلِيَآءَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۖ إِنَّ كَيۡدَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ كَانَ ضَعِيفًا
4:76.en: Those who believe do battle for the cause of Allah; and those who disbelieve do battle for the cause of idols. So fight the minions of the devil. Lo! the devil's strategy is ever weak

0ZnY8zKKkfc.speaker: adnan
0ZnY8zKKkfc.speaker_note: His usual bilingual Jumuah format (Arabic khutbah with English explanation); speaks as the masjid's imam who has watched the Ramadan attendance graph for years.
0ZnY8zKKkfc.title: First Week of Ramadan: Taking Advantage of the Peace
0ZnY8zKKkfc.one_line: Shaytan is chained in Ramadan; use the ceasefire to find the weaknesses he exploited all year and repair your defences.
0ZnY8zKKkfc.summary: Delivered on the second day of Ramadan 1447, this bilingual khutbah is built on the hadith that the devils are chained when Ramadan begins. The sheikh points to the overflowing masjid as evidence: Allah has changed something in the universe that you cannot see or touch but can feel in your heart. He then surveys how Shaytan works through the Quran: he threatens with poverty and commands immorality, he made great companions slip at Uhud by exploiting sins they had carried from before, he makes people forget Allah, and Iblis openly promised to incite, ride down and share in people's wealth and children. His image is a castle under siege: the enemy has spent eleven months finding tunnels and weak points, and Ramadan is a ceasefire of 28 days in which to inspect and repair the walls before he is released again. In the Arabic second khutbah he laments the yearly cycle of masjids that fill up and empty within a week, then gives five steps: renew the intention, identify the weaknesses Shaytan exploited, identify the weaknesses of the nafs itself (whatever you still do with Shaytan chained is on you), change the lifestyle and hours around which sins happen, and devote the month to the Quran as the salaf did.

outline.heading: Opening
The enemy who sees you
outline.gist: Children of Adam, do not let Shaytan tempt you as he expelled your parents from the Garden, stripping them to expose them; he and his tribe see you from where you do not see them (7:27).

outline.heading: The devils are chained
outline.gist: The hadith he grades sahih from Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah: on the first night of Ramadan the devils and rebellious jinn are chained, the gates of Paradise opened and those of Hell closed, and a caller calls the seeker of good to come forward and the seeker of evil to stop.

outline.heading: A change you feel with the heart
outline.gist: At no other time do people pour into the houses of Allah like this: last night every room was packed and people prayed outside. Allah changed something in the universe that you cannot see, touch or hear but can feel in your heart.

outline.heading: He threatens you with poverty
outline.gist: Shaytan threatens you with poverty and commands what is shameful, while Allah promises forgiveness and bounty (2:268).

outline.heading: Uhud: slipped through earlier sins
outline.gist: Those who turned back at Uhud were made to slip by Shaytan because of some of what they had earned (3:155): mistakes and sins held onto for months were openings in their castle walls, and he waited for the right moment to make great men turn their backs. Allah pardoned them.

outline.heading: He makes them forget Allah
outline.gist: Shaytan took hold of them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah (58:19): a takeover that happens through the weeks and months.

outline.heading: Iblis's challenge and Allah's reply
outline.gist: Iblis asked for respite until the Day of Judgment to bring Adam's descendants under his control; Allah told him to incite whom he could with his voice, assault them with his cavalry and infantry, share in their wealth and children and make them promises, but he has no authority over Allah's true servants (17:62-65).

outline.heading: 28 days to repair the castle walls
outline.gist: The war has gone on all year; the walls need repair. Go in and find the tunnels, openings and weaknesses he found, and fix them in the 28 days left before Allah unleashes him again.

outline.heading: Interlude
How did Iblis get in?
outline.gist: The devils who spent the year turning our good into evil and putting diseases of the heart into our worship have been turned away from us, so every Muslim must look at himself and ask how Iblis found a way in. Shaytan is your enemy, so take him as an enemy (35:6).

outline.heading: Where are they the rest of the year?
outline.gist: In the past two nights masajid across the earth overflowed with weeping, humble worshippers reciting the Quran; but where are they after Ramadan, and where were they before? Change what is inside us so he finds no way back when he returns.

outline.heading: Weak but persistent
outline.gist: The plot of Shaytan is weak (4:76), but he never gives up, returning again and again until you soften and spend long months without asking yourself about intention, envy, resentment, laziness, vanity or arrogance. Return to Allah this month.

outline.heading: The predictable Ramadan graph
outline.gist: He knows the attendance graph by heart: packed for three or four nights, half empty by the end of the first week, back for the start of the last ten, then back again on the 27th to 29th.

outline.heading: Don't be part of the cycle: renew your intention
outline.gist: This month is your peace and your opportunity. First step: go back to the intention you had a few days before Ramadan, when you told yourself this one would change you.

outline.heading: Identify the weaknesses Shaytan used
outline.gist: Second: do not be lenient with yourself about the fact that he had his way with us all year; he knew how to reach, provoke and distract us, so identify those weaknesses and work on them this month.

outline.heading: Identify the weaknesses of the nafs
outline.gist: Third: with Shaytan gone, what you do now is on you, the monster built inside. Fasting has weakened it, so write down what you still do: if you are still scrolling, clicking, messaging and distracted, that is you, not him.

outline.heading: Lifestyle changes are underrated
outline.gist: Fourth: with a bad lifestyle nothing can help you win; identify the hours when sins happen and fill them differently, sleep early, come to the masjid and attend what is offered.

outline.heading: Eat light and mind your socks
outline.gist: Do not overeat before taraweeh; it is unpleasant for those praying beside you, especially with garlic, and if your socks smell, take them off, wash your feet and pray without them. Fifth: the Quran, as the salaf turned to it.

outline.heading: Devote the month to the Quran
outline.gist: Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, Malik, Sufyan, Qatadah, al-Aswad and al-A'mash set aside hadith, fiqh and grammar in Ramadan and completed the Quran every ten, five or two nights or more; focus on the Quran, sujood and dua.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: Ramadan is a ceasefire: the enemy is restrained and the gates of Paradise opened, a change in the universe felt in the heart.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: The month is for repairing what the year damaged, not for a two-week burst of attendance; five steps to use it.

themes.label: Shaytan: his methods and how to resist him
themes.note: Shaytan sees us from where we cannot see him, exploits sins we already carry, and promised to incite and share in our wealth and children; he has no power over Allah's true servants. The Ramadan chaining is the chance to study how he got in.

themes.label: Sins, their causes and remedies
themes.note: Using Uhud (3:155), he argues that Shaytan slipped the companions through sins they had earned before; our own habitual sins are the openings in the castle wall.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Every Muslim must look at himself and ask how Iblis found a way in; write down the mistakes you made before Ramadan and what you are still doing now that he is chained.

themes.label: Tazkiyah: purifying and training the self
themes.note: With Shaytan removed, what remains is the nafs: the monster we built inside. Fasting weakens it, so now is the time to work on desires and to change the lifestyle and hours around which sins happen.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: First step: renew the intention you had a few days before Ramadan to make this one count and to change yourself.

themes.label: The masjid: its role and etiquette
themes.note: The yearly cycle of a packed then emptying masjid; also practical etiquette (do not overeat before taraweeh, wash your feet and remove smelly socks).

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: The salaf put aside hadith, fiqh and grammar in Ramadan and completed the Quran every ten, five or two nights; the month is for concentrated Quran, sujood and dua.

quran.point: Children of Adam, do not let Shaytan tempt you as he expelled your parents; he and his tribe see you from where you do not see them.
Shaytan threatens you with poverty and commands immorality while Allah promises forgiveness and bounty.
Those who turned back at Uhud were made to slip by Shaytan because of some of what they had earned; sins become his openings.
Shaytan overcame them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah.
Iblis asks for time to lead Adam's descendants astray, Allah tells him to incite and share in their wealth and children, but he has no authority over Allah's servants.
Shaytan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy; he only calls his party to the Blaze.
The plot of Shaytan is weak; he wins only by persistence, coming again and again until you give in.

hadith.gist: When the first night of Ramadan comes the devils and rebellious jinn are chained, the gates of Hell are closed and none opened, the gates of Paradise are opened and none closed, and a caller calls: seeker of good, come forward; seeker of evil, desist.
hadith.source: Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah (he grades the chain sahih)

maxims: Shaytan found tunnels in your castle walls
You have 28 days to fix your defences
What you do now is on you, not him
Don't be a part of the cycle
Lifestyle changes are underrated

stories.who: The companions at Uhud (3:155)
stories.point: Great men turned their backs because Shaytan exploited weaknesses they already had; he waits for the right moment to use old sins.

stories.who: Iblis's challenge to Allah (17:62-65)
stories.point: Shaytan announced his plan openly: incite, assault, share in wealth and children, make false promises; Allah's true servants are beyond his authority.

stories.who: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, Malik, Sufyan, Qatadah, Al-Aswad and Al-A'mash in Ramadan
stories.point: The salaf set aside hadith, fiqh and grammar when Ramadan came and devoted themselves to the Quran, completing it every ten, five, two or one nights.

contemporary: Overflow crowds at the London masjid in the first nights of Ramadan 1447: closed rooms opened and people praying outside in the cold
Scrolling, clicking and messaging as the habits of the nafs that continue even with Shaytan chained
takeaways: Renew the intention you had before Ramadan to make this month the one that changes you
Identify the specific weaknesses Shaytan exploited during the year and write them down
Identify the weaknesses of your own nafs: whatever you still do while Shaytan is chained is your own habit, so work on it now
Make lifestyle changes: sleep early, change what you do at the hours when sins happen, come to the masjid, eat less before prayer
Devote the rest of the month to the Quran, sujood and dua as the salaf did, and do not drop off after the first week

4:65.ar: فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ حَتَّىٰ يُحَكِّمُوكَ فِيمَا شَجَرَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُواْ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ حَرَجࣰ ا مِّمَّا قَضَيۡتَ وَيُسَلِّمُواْ تَسۡلِيمࣰ ا
4:65.en: But nay, by thy Lord, they will not believe (in truth) until they make thee judge of what is in dispute between them and find within themselves no dislike of that which thou decidest, and submit with full submission

4:71.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ خُذُواْ حِذۡرَكُمۡ فَٱنفِرُواْ ثُبَاتٍ أَوِ ٱنفِرُواْ جَمِيعࣰ ا
4:71.en: O ye who believe! Take your precautions, then advance the proven ones, or advance all together

4:72.ar: وَإِنَّ مِنكُمۡ لَمَن لَّيُبَطِّئَنَّ فَإِنۡ أَصَٰبَتۡكُم مُّصِيبَةࣱ قَالَ قَدۡ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيَّ إِذۡ لَمۡ أَكُن مَّعَهُمۡ شَهِيدࣰ ا
4:72.en: Lo! among you there is he who loitereth; and if disaster overtook you, he would say: Allah hath been gracious unto me since I was not present with them

4:73.ar: وَلَئِنۡ أَصَٰبَكُمۡ فَضۡلࣱ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لَيَقُولَنَّ كَأَن لَّمۡ تَكُنۢ بَيۡنَكُمۡ وَبَيۡنَهُۥ مَوَدَّةࣱ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي كُنتُ مَعَهُمۡ فَأَفُوزَ فَوۡزًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
4:73.en: And if a bounty from Allah befell you, he would surely cry, as if there had been no love between you and him: Oh, would that I had been with them, then should I have achieved a great success

4:160.ar: فَبِظُلۡمࣲ مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ حَرَّمۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ طَيِّبَٰتٍ أُحِلَّتۡ لَهُمۡ وَبِصَدِّهِمۡ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ كَثِيرࣰ ا
4:160.en: Because of the wrongdoing of the Jews We forbade them good things which were (before) made lawful unto them, and because of their much hindering from Allah's way

4:161.ar: وَأَخۡذِهِمُ ٱلرِّبَوٰاْ وَقَدۡ نُهُواْ عَنۡهُ وَأَكۡلِهِمۡ أَمۡوَٰلَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡبَٰطِلِۚ وَأَعۡتَدۡنَا لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ مِنۡهُمۡ عَذَابًا أَلِيمࣰ ا
4:161.en: And of their taking usury when they were forbidden it, and of their devouring people's wealth by false pretences, We have prepared for those of them who disbelieve a painful doom

4:162.ar: لَّٰكِنِ ٱلرَّٰسِخُونَ فِي ٱلۡعِلۡمِ مِنۡهُمۡ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبۡلِكَۚ وَٱلۡمُقِيمِينَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَۚ وَٱلۡمُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ سَنُؤۡتِيهِمۡ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمًا
4:162.en: But those of them who are firm in knowledge and the believers believe in that which is revealed unto thee, and that which was revealed before thee, especially the diligent in prayer and those who pay the poor-due, the believers in Allah and the Last Day. Upon these We shall bestow immense reward

2:184.ar: أَيَّامࣰ ا مَّعۡدُودَٰتࣲۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرࣲ فَعِدَّةࣱ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۚ وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُۥ فِدۡيَةࣱ طَعَامُ مِسۡكِينࣲۖ فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرࣰ ا فَهُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّهُۥۚ وَأَن تَصُومُواْ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:184.en: (Fast) a certain number of days; and (for) him who is sick among you, or on a journey, (the same) number of other days; and for those who can afford it there is a ransom: the feeding of a man in need - but whoso doeth good of his own accord, it is better for him: and that ye fast is better for you if ye did but know

33:36.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنࣲ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:36.en: And it becometh not a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His messenger have decided an affair (for them), that they should (after that) claim any say in their affair; and whoso is rebellious to Allah and His messenger, he verily goeth astray in error manifest

3:75.ar: ۞وَمِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مَنۡ إِن تَأۡمَنۡهُ بِقِنطَارࣲ يُؤَدِّهِۦٓ إِلَيۡكَ وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ إِن تَأۡمَنۡهُ بِدِينَارࣲ لَّا يُؤَدِّهِۦٓ إِلَيۡكَ إِلَّا مَا دُمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ قَآئِمࣰ اۗ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ قَالُواْ لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡنَا فِي ٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ سَبِيلࣱ وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡكَذِبَ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ
3:75.en: Among the People of the Scripture there is he who, if thou trust him with a weight of treasure, will return it to thee. And among them there is he who, if thou trust him with a piece of gold, will not return it to thee unless thou keep standing over him. That is because they say: We have no duty to the Gentiles. They speak a lie concerning Allah knowingly

7jO_li_9whc.speaker: adnan
7jO_li_9whc.speaker_note: Sheikh Adnan's Ramadan Quranic Themes series; speaks of his son Ahmed and his own village back home
7jO_li_9whc.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 5: Quranic Themes 2 - Istiqamah and Moral Absolutism
7jO_li_9whc.one_line: Incorruptibility as a Quranic theme: small ethical breaches grow, faith means accepting all of Allah's rulings, and principle, not odds, decides a believer's stand.
7jO_li_9whc.summary: He presents istiqama, upright steadfastness, as incorruptibility: holding to a moral standard while self-interest constantly pulls toward bending rules. Ethical breaches, unlike ordinary mistakes, are not fixed by an apology or a fatwa; the only way out is to go back, admit it, correct it and bear the consequences. Corruption grows from tiny steps, a candy bar before embezzlement, a lingering look before zina, cheating in school before a collapsed building, and even the crimes in the Epstein files began that way. Reviving Islam, for him, means reviving its values, as the Prophet was ethically impeccable. From An-Nisa he draws three forms of corruption. First, cherry-picking Allah's rulings, as people who welcomed the Prophet's teachings but not his judgment did, and as many still sidestep women's inheritance; a Muslim need not like every ruling but must accept all of them, and part-time 'Muslim consumers' weigh the community down. Second, the fair-weather believer who lags behind and waits to see who wins; he illustrates the pull of winners with his own football loyalties and says Islam is not a strategy. Third, the earlier community that took usury from outsiders, a small compromise whose compounding fruit is today's debt, inflation and inequality. He asks the young especially to decide now that they will not be corrupt.

outline.heading: Counted days slip through your fingers
outline.gist: Ramadan's numbered days pass before we take care of them, and no one knows whether another year is promised.

outline.heading: Interlude
Istiqama as incorruptibility
outline.gist: A major Quranic theme: being a straight shooter with oneself and others while life constantly pulls toward corruption.

outline.heading: Ethical dilemmas have no easy fatwa
outline.gist: Rulings are easy to answer, but a dilemma that already contains two ethical breaches has no fix except undoing them, which people do not want to hear.

outline.heading: Mistakes need apology; breaches need reversal
outline.gist: An honest mistake is forgiven with an apology, but an ethical breach requires admitting it, correcting it and living with the consequences.

outline.heading: Corruption grows from small breaches
outline.gist: Embezzlers start with a candy bar or a parent's wallet and people fall into zina after years of small steps; nobody's first time comes from nowhere.

outline.heading: Reviving Islam means reviving its values
outline.gist: His priority is not political governance or punishments but bringing back justice, honesty, trustworthiness, loyalty and accountability.

outline.heading: The Prophet was ethically impeccable
outline.gist: Before anything else he never breached his moral standard and kept only ethically sound people around him, which Islamic work still requires.

outline.heading: Cheating in school leads to collapsed buildings
outline.gist: A student who cheats keeps cheating through university and career until someone loses an opportunity or a building fails.

outline.heading: The Epstein files began with small steps
outline.gist: No one is born aiming for such crimes; they are the end point of small ethical breaches left unchecked.

outline.heading: Find the weak spots in your armour
outline.gist: The young should decide now that they will not be corrupt and watch the areas where Shaytan whispers that a small breach is no big deal.

outline.heading: They will not believe until they make you judge
outline.gist: Some around the Prophet liked his teachings but wanted to settle their own disputes; Allah swears they have no faith until they seek his judgment.

outline.heading: Islam's justice: the accuser must bring proof
outline.gist: Where nobles' accusations once convicted the weak, Islam put the burden of proof on the accuser and gave the slandered recourse.

outline.heading: Inheritance rulings still dodged
outline.gist: Families pressure women to give up their shares; when a rule required them to receive the inheritance first, not one woman in his village gave it back.

outline.heading: No resentment, full submission
outline.gist: Faith requires finding no ill feeling about the judgment and submitting to it completely.

outline.heading: Picking and choosing is corruption
outline.gist: Accepting some of Allah's commands and refusing others breaks the pledge of the shahadah; a believer has no choice once Allah decides.

outline.heading: You need not like a ruling, but you must accept it
outline.gist: There are no discounts on the deen; only the heart of a wali delights in every ruling, but every Muslim must accept even the inconvenient ones.

outline.heading: No part-time Muslims
outline.gist: Community members who appear only to demand service are dead weight; falling short in practice is normal, refusing a ruling is not.

outline.heading: The one who lags behind and waits
outline.gist: When called to mobilize some hang back; if disaster strikes they thank Allah they were absent, and if there is gain they wish they had been there, as if no bond existed.

outline.heading: In it only for the good times
outline.gist: The corrupt side with whoever is strong and disown the group the moment it weakens.

outline.heading: A believer acts on principle, not odds
outline.gist: The believer mobilizes whether the enemy is weak or overwhelming, because the outcome does not decide what is right.

outline.heading: Muslim because it is right, not convenient
outline.gist: Faith that depends on being surrounded and protected by Muslims will collapse when circumstances change.

outline.heading: People worship winners: a football confession
outline.gist: He supports Manchester United because they dominated his 1990s childhood, while his son chose Manchester City; fine for sport, fatal for principles.

outline.heading: Islam is not a strategy
outline.gist: Belief is a choice held for life whether surrounded by millions of Muslims or none.

outline.heading: The hypocrite's gamble and the believer's one question
outline.gist: The leader of the hypocrites held back a third of the army at Uhud and later claimed credit; the believer only asks what the right thing to do is.

outline.heading: Good things forbidden for wrongdoing and usury
outline.gist: An earlier community lost lawful things for their oppression, for barring others from Allah's path, for taking usury and devouring people's wealth.

outline.heading: Those firm in knowledge among them
outline.gist: Those truly grounded in the Torah and the believers who pray, give zakat and believe in the Last Day are promised a great reward.

outline.heading: Following in their footsteps: usury with outsiders
outline.gist: These stories warn us not to repeat their mistakes, such as allowing usury with outsiders while forbidding it among themselves.

outline.heading: The compounding cost of a small breach
outline.gist: National debt, inflation, unaffordable housing, wars and inequality show where a 'little' usury leads; Shaytan is patient and works over centuries.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Istiqamah: incorruptibility, steadfastness, moral integrity
themes.note: Incorruptibility is the thread of the talk, illustrated through three forms of corruption in An-Nisa.

themes.label: Sins, their causes and remedies
themes.note: Ethical breaches start small, grow unless reversed, and require restitution, not just an apology.

themes.label: Values, principles and ethics as a system
themes.note: Reviving Islam means reviving its ethical values, modelled by the Prophet's impeccable conduct.

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: Faith requires accepting all of Allah's rulings without resentment, even the ones we dislike.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Islam's burden of proof and inheritance rules protected the weak, and people still try to evade them.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: Part-time members who only show up to demand service weaken the community.

themes.label: Hypocrisy (nifaq)
themes.note: The fair-weather believer who waits to see who wins, embodied by the leader of the hypocrites at Uhud.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Usury and unlawful taking of wealth compound into today's debt, inflation and inequality.

takeaways: When you commit an ethical breach, go back, admit it, correct it and accept the consequences instead of seeking a loophole.

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

2:31.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِي بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:31.en: And He taught Adam all the names, then showed them to the angels, saying: Inform Me of the names of these, if ye are truthful

2:32.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلۡمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمۡتَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
2:32.en: They said: Be glorified! We have no knowledge saving that which Thou hast taught us. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower, the Wise

2:33.ar: قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ أَنۢبِئۡهُم بِأَسۡمَآئِهِمۡۖ فَلَمَّآ أَنۢبَأَهُم بِأَسۡمَآئِهِمۡ قَالَ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكُمۡ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ غَيۡبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَأَعۡلَمُ مَا تُبۡدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمۡ تَكۡتُمُونَ
2:33.en: He said: O Adam! Inform them of their names, and when he had informed them of their names, He said: Did I not tell you that I know the secret of the heavens and the earth? And I know that which ye disclose and which ye hide

2:34.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأٓدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:34.en: And when We said unto the angels: Prostrate yourselves before Adam, they fell prostrate, all save Iblis. He demurred through pride, and so became a disbeliever

2:35.ar: وَقُلۡنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسۡكُنۡ أَنتَ وَزَوۡجُكَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنۡهَا رَغَدًا حَيۡثُ شِئۡتُمَا وَلَا تَقۡرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:35.en: And We said: O Adam! Dwell thou and thy wife in the Garden, and eat ye freely (of the fruits) thereof where ye will; but come not nigh this tree lest ye become wrong-doers

2:36.ar: فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ عَنۡهَا فَأَخۡرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِۖ وَقُلۡنَا ٱهۡبِطُواْ بَعۡضُكُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ عَدُوࣱّۖ وَلَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مُسۡتَقَرࣱّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينࣲ‏
2:36.en: But Satan caused them to deflect therefrom and expelled them from the (happy) state in which they were; and We said: Fall down, one of you a foe unto the other! There shall be for you on earth a habitation and provision for a time

2:37.ar: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتࣲ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:37.en: Then Adam received from his Lord words (of revelation), and He relented toward him. Lo! He is the relenting, the Merciful

2:38.ar: قُلۡنَا ٱهۡبِطُواْ مِنۡهَا جَمِيعࣰ اۖ فَإِمَّا يَأۡتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدࣰ ى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ فَلَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ
2:38.en: We said: Go down, all of you, from hence; but verily there cometh unto you from Me a guidance; and whoso followeth My guidance, there shall no fear come upon them neither shall they grieve

2:39.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَكَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
2:39.en: But they who disbelieve, and deny Our revelations, such are rightful Peoples of the Fire. They will abide therein

2:92.ar: ۞وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَكُم مُّوسَىٰ بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ ثُمَّ ٱتَّخَذۡتُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ وَأَنتُمۡ ظَٰلِمُونَ
2:92.en: And Moses came unto you with clear proofs (of Allah's Sovereignty), yet, while he was away, ye chose the calf (for worship) and ye were wrong-doers

2:93.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِيثَٰقَكُمۡ وَرَفَعۡنَا فَوۡقَكُمُ ٱلطُّورَ خُذُواْ مَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةࣲ وَٱسۡمَعُواْۖ قَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا وَعَصَيۡنَا وَأُشۡرِبُواْ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ بِكُفۡرِهِمۡۚ قُلۡ بِئۡسَمَا يَأۡمُرُكُم بِهِۦٓ إِيمَٰنُكُمۡ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
2:93.en: And when We made with you a covenant and caused the Mount to tower above you, (saying): Hold fast by that which We have given you, and hear (Our Word), they said: We hear and we rebel. And (worship of) the calf was made to sink into their hearts because of their rejection (of the covenant). Say (unto them): Evil is that which your belief enjoineth on you, if ye are believers

2:94.ar: قُلۡ إِن كَانَتۡ لَكُمُ ٱلدَّارُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَالِصَةࣰ مِّن دُونِ ٱلنَّاسِ فَتَمَنَّوُاْ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:94.en: Say (unto them): If the abode of the Hereafter in the providence of Allah is indeed for you alone and not for others of mankind (as ye pretend), then long for death (for ye must long for death) if ye are truthful

2:95.ar: وَلَن يَتَمَنَّوۡهُ أَبَدَۢا بِمَا قَدَّمَتۡ أَيۡدِيهِمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:95.en: But they will never long for it, because of that which their own hands have sent before them. Allah is aware of evil-doers

2:96.ar: وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمۡ أَحۡرَصَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ حَيَوٰةࣲ وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشۡرَكُواْۚ يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمۡ لَوۡ يُعَمَّرُ أَلۡفَ سَنَةࣲ وَمَا هُوَ بِمُزَحۡزِحِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ أَن يُعَمَّرَۗ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرُۢ بِمَا يَعۡمَلُونَ
2:96.en: And thou wilt find them greediest of mankind for life and (greedier) than the idolaters. (Each) one of them would like to be allowed to live a thousand years. And to live (a thousand years) would be no means remove him from the doom. Allah is Seer of what they do

2:124.ar: ۞وَإِذِ ٱبۡتَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ رَبُّهُۥ بِكَلِمَٰتࣲ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّۖ قَالَ إِنِّي جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامࣰ اۖ قَالَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِيۖ قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهۡدِي ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:124.en: And (remember) when his Lord tried Abraham with (His) commands, and he fulfilled them, He said: Lo! I have appointed thee a leader for mankind. (Abraham) said: And of my offspring (will there be leaders)? He said: My covenant includeth not wrong-doers

20:120.ar: فَوَسۡوَسَ إِلَيۡهِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلۡخُلۡدِ وَمُلۡكࣲ لَّا يَبۡلَىٰ
20:120.en: But the devil whispered to him, saying: O Adam! Shall I show thee the tree of immortality and power that wasteth not away

7:23.ar: قَالَا رَبَّنَا ظَلَمۡنَآ أَنفُسَنَا وَإِن لَّمۡ تَغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَتَرۡحَمۡنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
7:23.en: They said: Our Lord! We have wronged ourselves. If thou forgive us not and have not mercy on us, surely we are of the lost

Qkj0rW5zlLs.speaker: adnan
Qkj0rW5zlLs.speaker_note: Sheikh Adnan's Ramadan Quranic Themes series; refers to his 13 years serving the community here
Qkj0rW5zlLs.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 1: Quranic Themes 2 - Stewardship
Qkj0rW5zlLs.one_line: Opening the second Quranic Themes series with stewardship (khilafah), read through Adam, the Children of Israel and Ibrahim in Al-Baqarah.
Qkj0rW5zlLs.summary: He opens the year's series by explaining that the Quran returns to themes rather than repeating itself, because a concept only lands when it is approached several times in different ways. The first theme is stewardship: the human being is a khalifa, not in a political sense but as someone left responsible for things on another's behalf, who will be asked how he cared for them. He reads three passages of Al-Baqarah as three kinds of steward. Adam failed his first test because he did not yet understand his own nafs and disliked being responsible, mortal and a servant; he repented with the words Allah gave him and never knowingly disobeyed again, and we are handed his lesson without paying his price. The Children of Israel are the example of failure: after clear signs they took the calf, said they hear and disobey, and their hearts were soaked in that love until it could not be removed; and they became greedy for mere life, a fear of death that makes a person sell out every principle. Ibrahim is the steward who passed test after test and was made an imam. He asks listeners to take responsibility seriously, use Ramadan to wash out sins that have settled in the heart, and rank values above survival.

outline.heading: The Quran teaches through themes, not repetition
outline.gist: The Quran revisits major and minor themes so a concept can be absorbed slowly; last year covered 29 themes and this year adds another set.

outline.heading: Stewardship as the human job description
outline.gist: A steward is responsible for something on someone else's behalf; the human being is a khalifa spiritually, not politically, and worships Allah through that responsibility and will be asked about it.

outline.heading: Interlude
Adam placed on earth as a khalifa
outline.gist: Adam begins like any of us, enjoying breath, food and companionship without yet knowing why, and is told he will be a steward on earth.

outline.heading: The tree: failing a test before knowing the self
outline.gist: Adam ate not out of evil or ingratitude but because he had not yet understood his nafs; Shaytan exploited this with the lie of immortality.

outline.heading: Three truths the nafs dislikes
outline.gist: Adam was uncomfortable being responsible, being mortal and being a servant, the same three things people resist today.

outline.heading: Sent down: shame and loss
outline.gist: On earth Adam lost safety, plenty and companionship, but what hurt most was the shame of having disobeyed Allah.

outline.heading: Words of repentance given to Adam
outline.gist: Not yet knowing what tawbah was, Adam was taught words to say, admitting he had wronged himself, and Allah accepted his repentance.

outline.heading: A scripted lesson, not a return to Paradise
outline.gist: Adam was still sent down because earth was his purpose; the episode teaches obedience, restraining the nafs and owning responsibility for oneself and one's family.

outline.heading: Follow the guidance; Adam never knowingly sinned again
outline.gist: Whoever follows Allah's guidance has nothing to fear; we receive the solved example for free, and Adam's later mistakes were only forgetfulness and lack of knowledge.

outline.heading: Interlude
Taking the calf after clear signs
outline.gist: Stewardship is both obligation and opportunity; Allah teaches it through good and failed examples, starting with a people who worshipped the calf after Musa's miracles.

outline.heading: The covenant under the raised mountain
outline.gist: Their covenant was renewed under the mountain; the Torah taught the same responsibility the Quran teaches, to shepherd the wellbeing of those around you.

outline.heading: Hearts soaked in the love of the calf
outline.gist: The word for 'made to drink' means soaked through; sin becomes deadly when it stays in the heart until it cannot be separated, like cloth left in perfume or sewage.

outline.heading: Ramadan can rid the heart of a soaked sin
outline.gist: A sin that persists despite knowing it is haram has been absorbed by the heart; Ramadan is a rare chance to remove it, and stewardship is impossible without doing so.

outline.heading: Greed for mere life
outline.gist: Being the most eager for life means a crippling fear of death; such a person will compromise any principle and cannot even trust himself to protect his own family.

outline.heading: A steward's priorities are values, in the right order
outline.gist: Muslims need to know not only Islam's values and ethics but how they rank, otherwise they discard a value that should never be dropped.

outline.heading: Our heroes stood their ground under threat
outline.gist: Prolonging life is not a value in itself; the people we honour held to their principles with a gun to their heads, which is what stewardship and manhood mean.

outline.heading: Three kinds of steward
outline.gist: Adam erred then got it right, the Children of Israel kept failing by choice, and Ibrahim got it right without the initial mistake.

outline.heading: Ibrahim tested with trial after trial
outline.gist: Ibrahim spoke against his people's idols, was thrown into the fire, expelled, debated star worshippers and a king, and passed every test.

outline.heading: Made an imam for mankind
outline.gist: Allah made him a leader; he died with few followers yet is now honoured by most of humanity, and he then asked about his descendants.

themes.label: Stewardship (khilafah) and human responsibility
themes.note: The human being is a khalifa responsible for self, family and community, and the three Baqarah passages show stewardship lived badly, recovered and done well.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Stewardship is presented as the answer to what we are here for beyond eating, drinking and greeting each other.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Adam's creation, test, fall and repentance read as a model lesson every person repeats.

themes.label: Tazkiyah: purifying and training the self
themes.note: Adam failed because he did not yet understand his nafs and its resistance to responsibility, mortality and servitude.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Allah taught Adam the words of repentance, and after it Adam never knowingly crossed the line again.

themes.label: Sins, their causes and remedies
themes.note: A sin left in the heart soaks into it until it cannot be removed, which is how addiction to sin forms.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: Ramadan is one of the few opportunities to wash out a sin the heart has absorbed.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: Greed for life is a fear of death that makes a person compromise every principle and untrustworthy as a steward.

themes.label: Values, principles and ethics as a system
themes.note: Muslims must know Islam's values and their ranking so they do not replace a higher value with a lower one.

themes.label: Courage and commitment
themes.note: The people we honour held their ground even at the cost of their lives.

quran.point: Shaytan's lie that the tree would bring immortality
The words of repentance Adam and his wife were taught: we have wronged ourselves

maxims: The Quran is not repetition; it is a thematic approach
Saying it once never works
You're a khalifa: not politically, but spiritually and humanely
The problem with sin is that it stays in your heart
If just living is your priority, you cannot be trusted

stories.who: Adam and the tree
stories.point: Failure came from not understanding the nafs; repentance and never knowingly repeating the sin is the path back.

stories.who: The Children of Israel and the golden calf
stories.point: A sin left to soak in the heart and an obsession with survival strip a people of their ability to be stewards.

stories.who: Ibrahim's trials
stories.point: Passing test after test earns leadership and a legacy far larger than one's following in life.

takeaways: See yourself as a steward who will be asked how you cared for yourself, your family and your community.
Use Ramadan to uproot a sin that has settled in your heart before it becomes permanent.
When you slip, repent as Adam did and never knowingly return to the same sin.
Do not let fear of death or love of comfort push you to compromise your principles.
Learn the values of Islam and their order of priority so you argue from the right ethic.

36:3.en: Lo! thou art of those sent

36:5.en: A revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful

36:6.ar: لِتُنذِرَ قَوۡمࣰ ا مَّآ أُنذِرَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ فَهُمۡ غَٰفِلُونَ
36:6.en: That thou mayst warn a folk whose fathers were not warned, so they are heedless

36:7.ar: لَقَدۡ حَقَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ عَلَىٰٓ أَكۡثَرِهِمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
36:7.en: Already hath the judgment, (for their infidelity) proved true of most of them, for they believe not

36:8.ar: إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَا فِيٓ أَعۡنَٰقِهِمۡ أَغۡلَٰلࣰ ا فَهِيَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَذۡقَانِ فَهُم مُّقۡمَحُونَ
36:8.en: Lo! We have put on their necks carcans reaching unto the chins, so that they are made stiff-necked

36:9.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا مِنۢ بَيۡنِ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ سَدࣰّ ا وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِمۡ سَدࣰّ ا فَأَغۡشَيۡنَٰهُمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُبۡصِرُونَ
36:9.en: And We have set a bar before them and a bar behind them, and (thus) have covered them so that they see not

36:10.ar: وَسَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَأَنذَرۡتَهُمۡ أَمۡ لَمۡ تُنذِرۡهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
36:10.en: Whether thou warn them or thou warn them not, it is alike for them, for they believe not

36:11.ar: إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلذِّكۡرَ وَخَشِيَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِۖ فَبَشِّرۡهُ بِمَغۡفِرَةࣲ وَأَجۡرࣲ كَرِيمٍ
36:11.en: Thou warnest only him who followeth the Reminder and feareth the Beneficent in secret. To him bear tidings of forgiveness and a rich reward

36:12.ar: إِنَّا نَحۡنُ نُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ وَنَكۡتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُواْ وَءَاثَٰرَهُمۡۚ وَكُلَّ شَيۡءٍ أَحۡصَيۡنَٰهُ فِيٓ إِمَامࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
36:12.en: Lo! We it is Who bring the dead to life. We record that which they send before (them, and their footprints. And all things We have kept in a clear Register)

7:179.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ذَرَأۡنَا لِجَهَنَّمَ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِۖ لَهُمۡ قُلُوبࣱ لَّا يَفۡقَهُونَ بِهَا وَلَهُمۡ أَعۡيُنࣱ لَّا يُبۡصِرُونَ بِهَا وَلَهُمۡ ءَاذَانࣱ لَّا يَسۡمَعُونَ بِهَآۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ كَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ بَلۡ هُمۡ أَضَلُّۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡغَٰفِلُونَ
7:179.en: Already have We urged unto hell many of the jinn and humankind, having hearts wherewith they understand not, and having eyes wherewith they see not, and having ears wherewith they hear not. These are as the cattle - nay, but they are worse! These are the neglectful

iotn5F9qYSA.speaker: adnan
iotn5F9qYSA.speaker_note: first-person weekend tafseer series he runs every year; refers to his medical work
iotn5F9qYSA.title: Tafseer of Surat Yasin, Part 1 (1-12)
iotn5F9qYSA.one_line: Opening the Yasin series: obedience to Allah as the source of real life, wisdom over mere knowledge, and the shackles of heedlessness.
iotn5F9qYSA.summary: He opens his annual weekend tafseer with Surat Yasin, placing it in a cluster of surahs about submission to Allah. He argues the surah's link with death comes less from a weak narration than from its theme: obedience is what gives the spirit real life, so some people under the ground are more alive than people walking above it. Drawing on quality-of-life calculations from oncology, he says the Quran cared about how well we live long before medicine did. He explains the opening letters, the late Meccan setting of persecution, and his three dimensions of any surah, the third being the reader. The oath by the wise Quran leads to a distinction between knowledge and wisdom: knowledge without purpose produces bombs, war and waste. The core problem the surah names is heedlessness, failing to see what is right in front of you, illustrated by the image of hands shackled to the chin with eyes forced upward. He warns Muslims that this can be their state too, especially toward family. Guidance cannot be forced; only those already searching can be warned. He closes on Allah reviving dead hearts and recording what people leave behind, and urges never losing hope in oneself or others.

outline.heading: Yasin within a cluster of surahs on submission
outline.gist: He introduces the series and places Yasin among surahs that each examine obedience to Allah from a different angle, individual and communal.

outline.heading: Why Yasin is associated with death
outline.gist: Reciting Yasin over the dead rests on a narration with a weak chain; he suggests the association really comes from the surah's theme.

outline.heading: Obedience as the life of the spirit
outline.gist: True life comes from submission to Allah; some people under the ground are more alive than those walking above it.

outline.heading: Quality of life, not just length of life
outline.gist: Using oncology's quality-of-life calculations, he says the Quran asked whether we are truly alive long before medicine did.

outline.heading: Ya-Sin: the separated letters as a challenge
outline.gist: The letters remind the Arabs that the Quran is made of the same letters as their poetry, so let them produce something like it.

outline.heading: Ya-Sin as a name of the Prophet
outline.gist: A widely accepted view treats Ya-Sin as a name of the Prophet; Imam Malik was cautious about naming children with it.

outline.heading: First dimension: revealed in the late Meccan years of persecution
outline.gist: He lays out the four periods of revelation and places Yasin in the late Meccan period, when the companions were at their weakest.

outline.heading: Second dimension: its place in the mushaf
outline.gist: Where the surah sits in the Quran, within its cluster, tells you what it is about.

outline.heading: Third dimension: you, the reader
outline.gist: Your experience, understanding and application of the surah complete it.

outline.heading: Oath by the wise Quran: wisdom versus knowledge
outline.gist: Wisdom is knowing when and how to apply knowledge toward an outcome; knowledge alone is only information.

outline.heading: Knowledge without purpose
outline.gist: Humanity piles up knowledge, now with AI, without asking what it is for; stripped of wisdom it ends in bombs, war and inequality.

outline.heading: A messenger on a straight path, sent down by the Mighty, the Merciful
outline.gist: The Prophet is on a straight path because the book came down to him from Allah.

outline.heading: Warning a heedless people: obliviousness as the barrier to life
outline.gist: Heedlessness is not a lack of knowledge but a lack of attentiveness to what is right in front of you.

outline.heading: Aiming far while neglecting family
outline.gist: Chasing big goals while neglecting family is not praiseworthy; the Prophet achieved more than anyone yet never neglected his family or friends.

outline.heading: A people whose fathers were never warned
outline.gist: The Meccans came from generations who lived between prophets and were oblivious to basics we now take for granted.

outline.heading: When it has not clicked yet
outline.gist: Heedlessness is almost unfixable from outside; he sees in young people's eyes whether it has clicked, and warns against speaking badly of those not there yet.

outline.heading: Shackles to the chin, heads forced upward
outline.gist: The image of hands chained up to the chin, eyes forced to the sky and barriers before and behind: people who cannot see what is in front of them.

outline.heading: The verse and the hijrah night story
outline.gist: The story that the Prophet recited this verse while leaving his house unseen lacks authenticity; the verse is about heedlessness, not protection.

outline.heading: Why they would not listen to a simple message
outline.gist: The Quran explains to the Prophet why a message so simple and complete was not registering: their state of mind, not the message.

outline.heading: This can be a Muslim's state too
outline.gist: Muslims can shackle themselves and miss their own mistakes and blessings; he wants this to bring some fear before something precious is taken away.

outline.heading: The Prophet unable to reach his own family
outline.gist: These verses comforted the Prophet, who carried the final message yet could not get his own relatives to listen.

outline.heading: Only those who follow the reminder can be warned
outline.gist: Guidance cannot be forced; it can be made available and attractive, but the person must already be searching.

outline.heading: Reverence for the Merciful in the unseen
outline.gist: The receptive person already senses someone worthy of reverence even before knowing who He is.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr was already there; seekers with no one to guide them
outline.gist: Abu Bakr accepted without hesitation; many seekers today find no one to present Islam because Muslims have not fully accepted it themselves.

outline.heading: From warning to good tidings
outline.gist: After repeated words of warning, the seeker is given good news of forgiveness and a noble reward.

outline.heading: We give life to the dead, literally and figuratively
outline.gist: Allah resurrects the dead and also revives dead hearts; people look for that life in fame, romance and success but find it only here.

outline.heading: Recording what they put forward and what they left behind
outline.gist: Life includes the consequences that continue after you are gone, and all of it is recorded.

outline.heading: Never lose hope in yourself or others
outline.gist: Since Allah gives life to the dead, no heart is beyond revival.

outline.heading: Imam mubin: a record worth putting forward
outline.gist: The record is called an imam, carrying the sense of leadership and something worth showing to humanity.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Obedience to Allah is what makes life worth living; quality of life matters more than length.

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: Yasin sits in a cluster of surahs that unpack what submitting to Allah actually means in practice.

themes.label: Seeking knowledge, learning and scholars
themes.note: Wisdom is knowledge directed to a goal; knowledge without purpose does harm.

themes.label: Heedlessness (ghaflah) and inattentiveness
themes.note: Obliviousness to what is right in front of you is the main barrier to a living heart, pictured as shackles that force the eyes upward.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Pursuing glory never excuses neglecting family; the Prophet never did.

themes.label: Guidance (hidayah)
themes.note: Guidance cannot be forced; only those already searching respond, like Abu Bakr.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: Many seekers find no one to present Islam because Muslims have not fully accepted it themselves.

themes.label: Hope, fear and the balance between them
themes.note: Allah revives dead hearts, so never lose hope; yet the shackles verses should bring some fear.

quran.point: Hearts that do not understand, eyes that do not see, ears that do not hear: like livestock or worse.
Another opening often understood as a name of the Prophet, like Ya-Sin.

hadith.gist: Reciting Yasin over the dead; he says the chain is weak and most scholars avoid narrating it.
Everyone the Prophet invited to Islam hesitated and thought it over except Abu Bakr, who accepted before he finished speaking.

maxims: Some under the ground are more alive than those above it
It's not how long you live, it's how well you live
You are the third dimension of any surah
Wisdom has an outcome; knowledge is just information
Guidance is not forced; you can only make it available

stories.who: Elderly in the Middle East reciting Yasin at graves
stories.point: A practice without strong evidence that reflects the surah's theme of true life.

stories.who: The hijrah night, the Prophet leaving his house unseen
stories.point: He rejects the story as unauthentic; the verse describes heedlessness, not a protection formula.

stories.who: Abu Bakr accepting Islam
stories.point: A heart already searching accepts the truth immediately.

contemporary: Quality-of-life calculations in oncology
AI and ever-growing databases of knowledge without purpose
Global warming, weapons and socioeconomic inequality
takeaways: Ask whether you are truly alive, not just how long you will live.
Pay attention to the blessings and people right in front of you, especially family.
Check yourself for heedlessness before something precious is taken away.
Do not speak badly of people who have not yet understood; you were once like them.
Never lose hope in yourself or others, since Allah revives dead hearts.
